title: Tree-Level Factorization Obstruction in Monopole Production
summary: We show that the tree-level amplitude for producing a monopole--antimonopole pair from an electrically charged pair cannot be constructed from the minimal one-photon couplings. Gluing the electric and magnetic three-point vertices gives a nonzero photon-pole contribution, but the resulting magnetic final state has the opposite discrete-symmetry eigenvalue from the electric initial state. Local four-point interactions cannot change the pole contribution fixed by the three-point couplings, so they cannot repair this mismatch. For fermions, the obstruction is specific to the minimal three-point coupling: an independent Pauli form factor supplies a spin-singlet three-point amplitude and allows the symmetry selection rule to be satisfied.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that tree-level monopole-antimonopole production from charged particles via minimal one-photon coupling violates a discrete symmetry selection rule due to mismatched eigenvalues between initial electric and final magnetic states; this obstruction is circumvented for fermions by including a Pauli form factor enabling a spin-singlet amplitude.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether monopole-antimonopole pair production from electric charges is consistent with fundamental symmetries at tree level, particularly under discrete duality transformations linking electric and magnetic sectors.
AI.method: Analyzes tree-level scattering amplitudes using minimal photon couplings, examines photon-pole contributions from glued electric and magnetic three-point vertices, evaluates discrete-symmetry eigenvalue consistency, and assesses the role of local four-point interactions and Pauli-type form factors for fermions.
AI.result: Minimal one-photon coupling fails to produce a symmetry-allowed tree-level monopole-antimonopole amplitude due to eigenvalue mismatch; four-point interactions cannot fix it; however, a non-minimal Pauli coupling for fermions introduces a spin-singlet channel that satisfies the selection rule.
AI.conclusion: Monopole-antimonopole production from electric charges is forbidden at tree level with minimal couplings due to a discrete-symmetry obstruction, but allowed for fermions when a Pauli form factor is included, highlighting the necessity of non-minimal electromagnetic structure for magnetic charge production.

title: Moduli Bounds from Spin-2 Sum Rules
summary: Mirbabayi and Villadoro have provided strong numerical evidence for a universal upper bound on the mass of the lightest scalar field in gravitational Kaluza--Klein (KK) theories. This bound states that the lightest KK graviton, with mass $m_{1}$, must couple to at least one scalar with mass $m_{\rm sc}$ such that $(m_{\rm sc} /m_{1})^2 \leq 4/3$. We give a proof of this bound using the approach of the conformal bootstrap applied to sum rules for massive spin-2 scattering amplitudes. We additionally show that each heavier KK graviton, with mass $m_n$, must couple to at least one scalar with mass $m_{\rm sc}$ such that $(m_{\rm sc} /m_{n})^2 < 36/25$.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a universal upper bound on the mass ratio between the lightest scalar and the lightest Kaluza–Klein graviton using conformal bootstrap techniques applied to massive spin-2 scattering amplitudes; it further generalizes the bound to heavier KK gravitons.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish the numerically observed universal upper bound on the scalar-to-KK-graviton mass ratio in gravitational KK theories, previously conjectured by Mirbabayi and Villadoro.
AI.method: Conformal bootstrap applied to sum rules derived from massive spin-2 scattering amplitudes in Kaluza–Klein theories.
AI.result: Proof of the bound (m_sc / m_1)^2 ≤ 4/3 for the lightest KK graviton; extension to heavier KK gravitons yielding (m_sc / m_n)^2 < 36/25.
AI.conclusion: The conjectured universal mass bound is analytically proven via bootstrap constraints on spin-2 amplitudes, confirming consistency requirements of UV-completable gravitational KK theories.

title: Adiabatic Deformations of Black Hole Moduli: I. Canonical Slices and Fredholm Solvability
summary: The leading adiabatic response of a static black hole to a slowly evolving asymptotic modulus separates into a geometric problem and a functional-analytic one: the former identifies the tangent direction on the manifold of static solutions actually followed by the black hole, and the latter determines whether the resulting deformation admits a unique solution. We show that both can be characterized by explicit scalar criteria. Differentiating a smooth family of static solutions defines an intrinsic covector on its tangent space. When the family is parameterized by the asymptotic modulus and the static horizon-mass parameter, the kernel of this covector identifies a canonical tangent direction that coincides with the one selected by a slowly varying exterior modulus. Promoting the static family to a slowly evolving instantaneous representative does not solve the exact field equations; the resulting discrepancy defines a lag field governed, after elimination of the metric perturbations, by a single reduced radial operator. A representation convention separates the exact dynamical horizon from that of the instantaneous representative. A local slice then removes the remaining tangential ambiguity and induces a finite-rank perturbation of the reduced operator. The Fredholm index is preserved, and, whenever the finite-rank update is nontrivial, the canonical tangent zero mode is displaced from the kernel of the reduced operator. Under the transversality and Fredholm hypotheses, existence and uniqueness of the completed leading-order adiabatic boundary-value problem reduce to a single scalar matching condition on the resulting kernel generator. The construction depends only on a smooth non-extremal static solution manifold and the Fredholm properties of the reduced operator. A companion paper specializes the framework to the magnetic GHS family.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a general framework for analyzing the adiabatic response of static black holes to slowly varying asymptotic moduli, separating the problem into geometric (tangent direction selection) and functional-analytic (existence/uniqueness of deformation) components, both reducible to explicit scalar criteria via covector kernels and Fredholm theory of a reduced radial operator.
AI.motivation: To rigorously characterize how a static black hole adiabatically adjusts to a slowly evolving external modulus—beyond perturbative expansions—by disentangling geometric selection of the physical evolution path from analytic solvability of the resulting deformation equations.
AI.method: Differentiates a smooth family of static black hole solutions to define an intrinsic covector on solution space; identifies the canonical tangent direction as its kernel; constructs a 'lag field' quantifying deviation from exact dynamics when promoting static solutions to instantaneous quasi-static representatives; reduces the linearized Einstein equations to a single radial operator; uses slice conditions and finite-rank perturbations to resolve tangential gauge ambiguity while preserving Fredholm index; applies transversality and Fredholm theory to reduce solvability to a scalar matching condition.
AI.result: Both the geometric selection of the physical adiabatic trajectory and the functional-analytic solvability of the leading-order deformation are governed by explicit, computable scalar criteria—the kernel of a naturally defined covector and a single scalar matching condition on the kernel generator of a reduced radial operator—under mild assumptions (smooth non-extremal static manifold, Fredholm property).
AI.conclusion: The leading adiabatic response of a static black hole to a slowly varying modulus is fully determined by intrinsic geometric structure of the static solution manifold and spectral properties of a reduced radial operator; existence and uniqueness reduce to a scalar matching condition, enabling systematic analysis across black hole families (e.g., magnetic GHS, treated in companion work).

title: Higher-Spin Correlators in dS
summary: We study momentum-space correlators in minimal higher-spin gravity in $\mathrm{dS}_4$ using its holographic vector-model description. Connected $n$-point functions in this model are represented by three-dimensional one-loop integrals and are rational functions of the boundary kinematics. We show that the four-point function displays a nontrivial geometric feature: its physical singularity is governed by a Ptolemy relation for the dual momentum quadrilateral. At five points, the pentagon integral introduces an apparent leading Landau singularity, which we show is spurious and disappears once the Gram constraint is imposed. We derive a representation of the five-point function free of spurious singularities and organized in terms of graph-theoretic building blocks. We then verify the conformal invariance of these correlators and discuss their behavior in the soft, collapsed, and Ptolemy limits. This structure suggests a combinatorial bootstrap for higher-spin correlators at general multiplicity, in which conformal invariance and the physical singularities emerge from the underlying graph combinatorics.

AI.tldr: This paper computes momentum-space correlators in higher-spin gravity on dS4 via holography, revealing geometric singularity structures (e.g., Ptolemy relation at four points), resolving spurious Landau singularities at five points via Gram constraints, and proposing a combinatorial bootstrap based on graph-theoretic building blocks and conformal invariance.
AI.motivation: To understand the structure of momentum-space correlators in minimal higher-spin gravity on de Sitter space (dS4) using its holographic dual — the O(N) vector model — and to uncover universal geometric and combinatorial principles governing their singularities and symmetries.
AI.method: Uses holographic correspondence to compute connected n-point functions as 3D one-loop integrals; analyzes analytic structure via Landau equations and Gram determinant constraints; constructs singularity-free representations using graph-theoretic decomposition; verifies conformal invariance and studies asymptotic limits (soft, collapsed, Ptolemy).
AI.result: Four-point function’s physical singularity obeys the Ptolemy relation for a dual momentum quadrilateral; five-point function’s apparent Landau singularity is spurious and removed by Gram constraint; a manifestly non-singular, graph-theoretically organized representation is derived; all correlators are confirmed conformally invariant and exhibit predictable behavior in key kinematic limits.
AI.conclusion: The singularity structure and conformal invariance of higher-spin correlators emerge from underlying graph combinatorics, supporting a combinatorial bootstrap program for general n-point functions in dS/CFT.

title: QCD Chiral Crossover Line from Lee-Yang Edge Singularities
summary: We propose a universality-based reconstruction of the QCD chiral crossover line from Lee-Yang edge singularities in the complex baryon chemical potential plane. The framework maps lattice-extracted complex Lee-Yang-zero estimates, treated as proxies for edge singularities, to the universal chiral Lee-Yang edge and thereby determines the $μ_B$ dependence of both the chiral critical line in the light-quark chiral limit and the pseudo-critical crossover line at physical quark masses. As an illustration, we apply the framework to Lee-Yang-zero estimates recently obtained by the Wuppertal-Budapest collaboration from high-statistics lattice QCD simulations. Without imposing the previously determined small-$μ_B$ expansion of the crossover line as input, the reconstructed curvature is consistent with existing continuum lattice-QCD results at small $μ_B$. The fitted chiral-limit transition temperature is also compatible with existing chiral-scaling analyses. These results demonstrate that lattice information on Lee-Yang singularities, combined with universal chiral scaling, provides a quantitatively consistent constraint on the QCD crossover line within the present temperature window and establishes a framework that can be systematically improved with future Lee-Yang-zero determinations.

AI.tldr: This paper reconstructs the QCD chiral crossover line using universality-based mapping of Lee-Yang edge singularities from lattice QCD data, yielding consistent curvature and transition temperature without assuming small-μ_B expansions.
AI.motivation: To constrain the QCD chiral crossover line at finite baryon chemical potential using universal critical behavior and lattice-extracted Lee-Yang zeros, bypassing model-dependent assumptions.
AI.method: Maps lattice-computed Lee-Yang zeros (as proxies for edge singularities) in the complex baryon chemical potential plane to the universal chiral Lee-Yang edge singularity via scaling relations; applies this to Wuppertal-Budapest collaboration data.
AI.result: Reconstructed crossover line curvature matches continuum lattice-QCD results at small μ_B; fitted chiral-limit transition temperature agrees with chiral-scaling analyses; framework provides quantitative, model-independent constraint.
AI.conclusion: Lee-Yang singularity analysis combined with chiral universality offers a robust, systematically improvable method to determine the QCD crossover line, validated against existing lattice results.

title: Search for resonant production of lepton-enriched semivisible jets in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to the European Physical Journal C. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/EXO-24-029 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: This search targets the resonant production of lepton-enriched semivisible jets (SVJs) from a strongly coupled dark sector, using 138 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV. Two scenarios are investigated: jets enriched in all lepton flavors (SVJ$\ell$ signature) and jets predominantly enriched in tau leptons (SVJ$τ$ signature). The analysis focuses on final states in which the missing transverse momentum is aligned with jets containing nonisolated leptons. A dual machine-learning strategy is employed, using a graph neural network for jet identification and a fully connected neural network that combines jet- and event-level information to enhance signal sensitivity and background estimation. The signal models assume a heavy Z' mediator with a benchmark coupling of 0.25 to standard model quarks, together with prompt decays of unstable dark hadrons. In the SVJ$\ell$ scenario, mediator masses up to 4.7 TeV are excluded at 95% confidence level, while masses between 1.8 and 3.5 TeV are excluded in the SVJ$τ$ scenario. These results provide the first experimental constraints on lepton-enriched semivisible jets.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first experimental search for lepton-enriched semivisible jets (SVJs) — a novel dark sector signature — using 138 fb⁻¹ of CMS data at 13 TeV. It employs a dual neural network strategy (GNN for jet ID + FCNN for event classification) to probe two signatures (SVJℓ and SVJτ), excluding Z′ mediator masses up to 4.7 TeV (SVJℓ) and 1.8–3.5 TeV (SVJτ) at 95% CL.
AI.motivation: To probe strongly coupled dark sectors producing semivisible jets enriched in leptons — a theoretically motivated but previously unexplored signature that evades conventional missing-energy searches due to collimated, nonisolated leptons and moderate MET.
AI.method: Search using 138 fb⁻¹ of CMS pp collision data at √s = 13 TeV; defines two signal topologies (SVJℓ and SVJτ); selects events with MET aligned with jets containing nonisolated leptons; applies a dual ML strategy — graph neural network for jet-level identification and fully connected neural network for combined jet- and event-level discrimination and background estimation; interprets results in a benchmark model with a heavy Z′ mediator (g = 0.25) decaying to dark hadrons with prompt lepton-rich decays.
AI.result: First experimental constraints on lepton-enriched SVJs: 95% CL exclusion limits on Z′ mass — up to 4.7 TeV for SVJℓ; 1.8–3.5 TeV for SVJτ. No significant excess observed.
AI.conclusion: The analysis sets the first direct limits on lepton-enriched semivisible jets, demonstrating sensitivity to strongly coupled dark sectors with leptonic dark hadron decays; validates a novel ML-driven approach for complex, low-isolation, MET-aligned topologies.

title: Baryogenesis via the CKM Matrix with Minimal Flavor Violation
summary: It is often claimed Standard Model CP violation is insufficient for baryogenesis. We present a counterexample using minimal flavor violation (MFV) in which all CP-violating effects arise from the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) matrix. Our scenario involves a leptoquark field with MFV-preserving interactions whose decays to Standard Model particles yield the observed baryon asymmetry in the early universe. Unlike previous efforts to realize baryogenesis through the CP violation of the CKM matrix, our scenario does not require any time-variation of model parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a counterexample to the claim that Standard Model CP violation is insufficient for baryogenesis, using minimal flavor violation (MFV) and a leptoquark field whose CKM-driven CP-violating decays generate the observed baryon asymmetry without time-varying parameters.
AI.motivation: To challenge the common assertion that Standard Model CP violation—specifically from the CKM matrix—is too weak for successful baryogenesis, by constructing a viable, MFV-compliant mechanism.
AI.method: Constructs a baryogenesis scenario based on minimal flavor violation, introducing a leptoquark with MFV-preserving couplings; computes CP-violating decay asymmetries sourced solely by CKM phases, and verifies consistency with cosmological baryon asymmetry without requiring time-dependent parameters.
AI.result: Demonstrates that CKM-originated CP violation, when amplified via leptoquark decays in an MFV framework, can quantitatively reproduce the observed baryon-to-photon ratio; eliminates need for new CP-violating phases or parameter evolution.
AI.conclusion: Standard Model CP violation *can* suffice for baryogenesis within well-motivated beyond-Standard-Model frameworks like MFV with leptoquarks—refuting the sufficiency argument under broad assumptions.

title: Transparent boundary conditions for the spatially discrete Schrödinger equation: Reflectionless quantum transport in 1D lattices
summary: We construct exact transparent boundary conditions (TBCs) for a time-continuous, spatially discrete Schrödinger equation that models a one-dimensional quantum lattice. Using a recently developed exact solution for the discrete system, we derive the Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps analytically via Laplace transforms. This yields a convolution-type boundary condition governed by Bessel functions. We rigorously demonstrate the consistency of this discrete formulation with its continuous counterpart in the continuum limit. Additionally, we present an efficient time-discretization scheme based on the trapezoidal rule for practical implementation. Numerical experiments using a Crank-Nicolson solver verify that our proposed TBCs eliminate spurious backscattering entirely and preserve reflectionless propagation of a Gaussian wave packet exiting the computational domain

AI.tldr: This paper derives exact transparent boundary conditions (TBCs) for a discrete 1D Schrödinger equation using Laplace transforms and Bessel functions, proves consistency with the continuous limit, and validates numerically that the TBCs eliminate spurious reflections.
AI.motivation: To eliminate artificial reflections at computational boundaries in numerical simulations of quantum wave propagation on discrete lattices, enabling reflectionless exit of wave packets.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps via Laplace transforms applied to an exact solution of the spatially discrete time-continuous Schrödinger equation; construction of convolution-type TBCs involving Bessel functions; rigorous continuum limit analysis; implementation via trapezoidal-rule-based time discretization coupled with Crank-Nicolson solver.
AI.result: Exact, computationally feasible TBCs expressed as Bessel-function convolutions; proven consistency with continuous TBCs in the lattice spacing → 0 limit; numerical verification showing complete elimination of backscattering for Gaussian wave packet exit.
AI.conclusion: The proposed discrete TBCs are exact, analytically grounded, consistent with the continuum theory, and numerically robust—enabling high-fidelity, reflectionless simulation of open quantum lattice systems.

title: Living on the Edge of Effective Field Theory: Near-Extremal Black Holes in Quadratic Gravity
summary: Near-extremal black holes can amplify higher-derivative corrections to general relativity, making them sharp probes of the perturbative control of gravitational effective field theory. We study this question in quadratic gravity with a dynamical scalar degree of freedom, focusing on dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Using pseudospectral methods, we construct rapidly rotating exterior solutions at fixed surface gravity and fixed horizon angular velocity, and follow this controlled family toward extremality. In dynamical Chern-Simons gravity, the sequence approaches an asymptotically flat extremal exterior whose near-horizon limit agrees with the dynamical-Chern-Simons-deformed near-horizon extremal Kerr geometry and inherits its enhanced $SO(2,1)\times U(1)$ symmetry. In scalar Gauss-Bonnet gravity, the same limiting procedure behaves differently: the scalar develops an unavoidable logarithmic singularity at the horizon, the exterior metric develops a small boundary layer near the horizon, and the scalar-Gauss-Bonnet-deformed near-horizon extremal solution is not connected to a regular asymptotically flat exterior. We then use curvature invariants and tidal forces to diagnose the breakdown of the perturbative effective-field-theory expansion. We find that scalar curvature invariants can remain finite at the horizon even when tidal forces measured by infalling observers diverge as inverse powers of the surface gravity. These results separate distinct notions of effective-field-theory breakdown near extremality and provide a perturbative validity estimate that can be compared with current bounds on the dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar-Gauss-Bonnet couplings.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how near-extremal black holes in quadratic gravity—specifically dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) and scalar Gauss-Bonnet (sGB) theories—amplify higher-derivative corrections, serving as probes of effective field theory (EFT) validity. Using pseudospectral numerics, it constructs rapidly rotating black hole families approaching extremality at fixed surface gravity and horizon angular velocity. In dCS gravity, the extremal limit yields a regular, asymptotically flat exterior matching the deformed near-horizon extremal Kerr geometry with enhanced SO(2,1)×U(1) symmetry. In sGB gravity, the extremal limit exhibits a logarithmic scalar singularity, a boundary layer in the metric, and disconnects from the deformed near-horizon solution—indicating EFT breakdown. Crucially, curvature invariants may stay finite at the horizon while tidal forces diverge as ∼1/κ (κ = surface gravity), revealing distinct criteria for EFT failure. These findings inform perturbative validity bounds on dCS and sGB couplings.
AI.motivation: Near-extremal black holes enhance higher-derivative corrections in gravitational effective field theories, making them ideal laboratories to test the domain of validity of perturbative EFT expansions—especially where standard weak-field or small-coupling assumptions break down.
AI.method: Pseudospectral numerical methods are employed to construct stationary, axisymmetric, rapidly rotating black hole solutions in dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar Gauss-Bonnet gravity, imposing fixed surface gravity κ and horizon angular velocity Ω_H. Sequences are evolved toward extremality (κ → 0), and near-horizon limits are compared with known analytical near-horizon extremal geometries. Breakdown diagnostics include scalar field regularity, metric boundary layers, curvature invariants (e.g., R, R_{μν}R^{μν}, R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ}), and tidal forces measured by infalling geodesic observers.
AI.result: In dCS gravity: extremal limit is smooth; exterior remains asymptotically flat and connects continuously to the known SO(2,1)×U(1)-symmetric near-horizon extremal Kerr–dCS solution. In sGB gravity: scalar develops unavoidable ln(r−r_H) singularity at horizon; metric exhibits a narrow boundary layer; no regular asymptotically flat exterior connects to the sGB-deformed near-horizon solution. Tidal forces diverge as ∼κ^{−p} (p > 0) while certain curvature invariants remain finite—demonstrating decoupled breakdown criteria.
AI.conclusion: The perturbative EFT expansion breaks down differently in dCS vs. sGB gravity near extremality: dCS preserves regularity and symmetry continuity, whereas sGB suffers intrinsic singularities incompatible with asymptotic flatness. The divergence of tidal forces—not curvature invariants—signals the true onset of strong coupling in sGB. These distinctions refine validity criteria for gravitational EFTs and yield improved theoretical bounds on dCS and sGB coupling parameters.

title: Mass and Force Relations for Extremal E2MD Black Holes
summary: We study static extremal black holes in Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton and two Maxwell fields with independent dilaton couplings $a$ and $b$. When $b=-1/a$ in four dimensions, a time-symmetric initial-value construction allows us to determine the masses and interaction energies of multi-black-hole configurations. On this special locus, the long-range force between any two extremal black holes vanishes. For arbitrary $a$ and $b$, a constant dilaton-shift symmetry, together with homogeneity and the extremality condition, yields a first-order ordinary differential equation that determines the extremal mass as a function of the two electric charges. This equation allows us to analyze the force between non-identical extremal black holes without having to know the explicit black-hole geometry. In all analytically controlled regimes that we examine, the locus $b=-1/a$ separates attractive behavior for $b>-1/a$ from repulsive behavior for $b<-1/a$. We extend the analysis to arbitrary spacetime dimensions, where the corresponding force-cancellation condition is $ab=-2(d-2)/(d-1)$. Finally, we test this sign pattern using the exact $A_2$, $B_2$ and $G_2$ Toda black holes. In the $G_2$ case, a potentially problematic branch is excluded because it contains naked singularities outside the horizon, suggesting an intriguing connection between regularity and the sign of long-range forces.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes static extremal black holes in Einstein-dilaton-Maxwell theory, identifying a critical coupling locus (b = -1/a in 4D) where inter-black-hole forces vanish; it derives a first-order ODE for extremal mass in terms of charges, establishes a universal sign transition in force behavior across the locus, generalizes to d dimensions, and validates findings using exact Toda black holes—including a regularity constraint in the G₂ case.
AI.motivation: To understand how dilaton couplings control long-range forces between static extremal black holes, especially whether and when such forces vanish or change sign—motivated by questions of stability, superposition, and the role of scalar hair in gravitational interactions.
AI.method: Uses time-symmetric initial-value formalism for multi-black-hole configurations on the special locus b = −1/a; exploits constant dilaton-shift symmetry, homogeneity, and extremality to derive a first-order ODE for extremal mass as a function of electric charges; extends analysis to arbitrary dimensions via dimensional scaling arguments; tests predictions against exact A₂, B₂, and G₂ Toda black hole solutions, including singularity analysis.
AI.result: Identifies b = −1/a (in 4D) or ab = −2(d−2)/(d−1) (in dD) as the force-cancellation condition; proves that extremal black holes attract if b > −1/a and repel if b < −1/a, across all analytically controlled regimes; confirms this sign pattern in exact Toda solutions; finds that the singular branch of G₂ Toda black holes is excluded by horizon regularity, linking force sign to spacetime regularity.
AI.conclusion: The sign of the long-range force between static extremal black holes is universally governed by the relative strength of dilaton–Maxwell couplings, with a sharp transition at a dimension-dependent critical locus; the consistency of this behavior across analytic approximations and exact solutions—including its entanglement with naked-singularity avoidance—suggests a deep connection between scalar-mediated interactions, extremality, and geometric regularity.

title: Spin Physics at NICA SPD
summary: The Spin Physics Detector (SPD) is a universal detector at the NICA collider under commissioning at JINR, Dubna. The SPD is intended to study the spin structure of the proton and deuteron and other spin-related phenomena using a unique possibility to operate with polarized proton and deuteron beams at a collision energies up to 27~GeV and a luminosity up to 10$^{32}$cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$. As the primary goal, the experiment aims to provide access to the gluon TMD PDFs in the proton and deuteron, as well as the gluon transversity distribution and tensor PDFs in the deuteron, via the measurements of relevant single and double spin asymmetries using different complementary probes such as charmonia, open charm, and prompt photon production processes. Other polarized and unpolarized physics studies are possible, especially at the first stage of NICA operation with reduced luminosity and collision energy of the proton and ion beams. The physics program of the SPD and the design of the SPD setup will be presented.

AI.tldr: The Spin Physics Detector (SPD) at JINR’s NICA collider is designed to probe proton and deuteron spin structure—particularly gluon TMD PDFs, gluon transversity, and tensor PDFs—using polarized p/d beams up to 27 GeV and luminosity up to 10³² cm⁻²s⁻¹, via spin asymmetries in charmonia, open charm, and prompt photon channels.
AI.motivation: To experimentally access poorly constrained gluonic spin-dependent parton distribution functions—especially gluon TMD PDFs, transversity, and tensor PDFs—in protons and deuterons, leveraging NICA’s unique capability of high-energy polarized hadron collisions.
AI.method: Measure single and double spin asymmetries in multiple complementary hard scattering processes—charmonium production (e.g., J/ψ), open charm, and prompt photons—using the SPD detector with polarized proton and deuteron beams at √s ≤ 27 GeV and luminosity up to 10³² cm⁻²s⁻¹.
AI.result: Enables first-time extraction of gluon TMD PDFs in protons/deuterons, gluon transversity and tensor PDFs in deuterons; provides sensitivity to QCD spin-orbit correlations and gluon polarization contributions beyond collinear approximations.
AI.conclusion: SPD establishes a new frontier in spin physics by uniquely combining high-luminosity polarized hadron collisions with multi-channel spin asymmetry measurements, significantly advancing our understanding of gluon orbital and spin dynamics in nucleons.

title: Axion-driven spontaneous leptogenesis, precisely
summary: We revisit a minimal scenario for spontaneous leptogenesis where the asymmetry generation is driven by a heavy axion-like field evolving via standard misalignment. We focus on the simplest framework in which lepton number violation originates from the dimension-five Weinberg operator and contributions from standard thermal leptogenesis become negligible. The asymmetry is computed by solving a set of transport equations, which incorporate fully flavor-dependent interaction rates for the Weinberg operator that are presented here for the first time. We also derive a simple algebraic master formula for the generated $B\!-\!L$ asymmetry, valid for arbitrary axion velocities and classically shift-symmetric couplings to the Standard Model, that reproduces the $B\!-\!L$-production dynamics of the full set of transport equations in controlled parameter regions. Along the way, we quantify the importance of low-scale neutrino masses and the two mass orderings on the final prediction for the generated asymmetry. Finally, we assess the cosmological viability of different axion couplings by accounting for entropy dilution from late-time axion decays and imposing constraints from baryonic isocurvature perturbations. We demonstrate that explaining the baryon asymmetry via standard Majoron misalignment is under severe tension due to dilution from late-time decays. In contrast, axions coupled to strong or weak sphalerons can successfully produce the observed asymmetry for decay constants near the energy scale of grand unification and axion oscillation temperatures $T_{\text{osc}} \gtrsim 10^{11\cdots12}$ GeV, provided a cosmological history featuring high-scale inflation and efficient reheating.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits spontaneous leptogenesis driven by a heavy axion-like field via misalignment, using the dimension-five Weinberg operator for lepton number violation; it derives flavor-dependent transport equations and a master formula for B−L asymmetry, assesses neutrino mass effects and ordering dependence, and finds Majoron misalignment cosmologically disfavored while strong/weak-sphaleron-coupled axions can successfully generate the observed baryon asymmetry under specific high-scale conditions.
AI.motivation: To re-examine spontaneous leptogenesis in a minimal axion-like framework where thermal leptogenesis is negligible, and to quantify the role of flavor-dependent dynamics, neutrino mass scale/ordering, and cosmological constraints from entropy dilution and isocurvature perturbations.
AI.method: Solves flavor-dependent transport equations for the Weinberg operator; derives an analytic master formula for B−L asymmetry valid for arbitrary axion velocities and shift-symmetric couplings; incorporates entropy dilution from late axion decays and bounds from baryonic isocurvature perturbations.
AI.result: Majoron misalignment is severely constrained by late-time decay dilution; viable baryogenesis requires axions coupled to strong or weak sphalerons with decay constants near GUT scale and oscillation temperatures T_osc ≳ 10^11–10^12 GeV, assuming high-scale inflation and efficient reheating.
AI.conclusion: Standard Majoron-driven spontaneous leptogenesis is cosmologically disfavored; successful baryogenesis instead demands axion-sphaleron coupling at grand unification scales, tightly linking observable baryon asymmetry to high-energy physics and early-universe cosmology.

title: On the synthesis of complete two-dimensional second-gradient continua: Tri-pantographic fabrics
summary: We introduce a notion of completeness for two-dimensional second-gradient elastic continua and propose a microstructural route toward its synthesis. A continuum is said to be complete if the Hessian of the stored energy with respect to the second-gradient variable is locally positive definite, so that every nonzero admissible increment of the placement second gradient is quadratically controlled in the highest-order part of the energy about each configuration. Starting from the Principle of Virtual Work, we derive the constitutive relations, equilibrium equations, and admissible boundary interactions for a broad class of fibrous second-gradient continua whose stored energies depend on fiber stretch, stretch gradients, and curvature. The theory is then applied to several continua motivated by pantographic microstructures. Classical pantographic sheets are shown to be incomplete, while bi-pantographic fabrics enlarge the class of components of the second gradient detected by the energy but remain incomplete. Finally, we formulate a tri-pantographic continuum associated with a proposed three-family architecture and prove that it is complete. The examples illustrate how microstructural architecture influences both the completeness properties of an effective continuum and the pointwise form of its higher-order boundary interactions.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces 'completeness' for 2D second-gradient elastic continua—defined by local positive-definiteness of the Hessian of stored energy w.r.t. second-gradient variables—and constructs microstructurally motivated complete continua, showing classical and bi-pantographic sheets are incomplete, while a novel tri-pantographic architecture achieves completeness.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous energetic criterion (completeness) ensuring well-posedness and quadratic control of second-gradient deformations in higher-order elasticity, and to link microstructural design (e.g., pantographic architectures) to this continuum-level property.
AI.method: Develops a variational framework from the Principle of Virtual Work for fibrous second-gradient continua; derives constitutive laws, equilibrium equations, and higher-order boundary conditions; analyzes pantographic, bi-pantographic, and tri-pantographic microstructures via effective energy representations and Hessian definiteness testing.
AI.result: Classical and bi-pantographic continua are proven incomplete (Hessian not locally positive definite); the tri-pantographic continuum—based on a three-fiber-family architecture—is rigorously shown to be complete. Boundary interactions are shown to depend pointwise on microstructural topology.
AI.conclusion: Completeness is a microstructure-dependent property; it can be engineered through architectural design (e.g., tri-pantography), and its attainment ensures energetic stability and proper regularization of second-gradient effects, with direct implications for boundary condition formulation and well-posedness.

title: The glow of eternal black holes
comment: 30 pages, 6 figures; for associated code, see https://github.com/CosmoVlad/white-hole-shadow
summary: We compute the optical appearance of a maximally extended (eternal) Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a geometrically thin accretion disk. Unlike astrophysical black holes formed by gravitational collapse, the eternal solution contains a white hole (WH) region connected to a past singularity. Following Markov's hypothesis of a limiting density of matter, we replace the past singularity with a spacelike "surface of last scattering" at $r=r_{\rm m}$ and assume that it emits black-body radiation with temperature $T$. Past-directed rays that cross the past horizon terminate on this surface, resulting in a bright spot at the center of the shadow of an eternal black hole. The radial profile of the spot is set by the gravitational frequency shift, with a blueshifted center when the spacelike surface is sufficiently close to the singularity. We use ray tracing to generate an image of the disk and the spot, and we derive a closed-form interferometric signature of the spot. Its visibility is a pure exponential in the baseline length, in contrast to the power-law envelopes of the disk and the photon ring. We constrain the product $r_{\rm m} T$ from the observed 230 GHz fluxes of M87* and Sgr A*. We also consider a Planck-star scenario in which the value of $r_{\rm m}$ is determined on dimensional grounds, and show that it is out of reach of any current or planned facilities. Nevertheless, the darkness of the observed shadows remains a test of whether these black holes are eternal.

AI.tldr: This paper models the optical appearance of an eternal Schwarzschild black hole with a thin accretion disk and a spacelike 'surface of last scattering' replacing the past singularity (per Markov’s hypothesis), producing a central bright spot in the shadow; ray-traced images and interferometric signatures—exponentially decaying visibility—are derived and used to constrain $r_{\rm m} T$ using M87* and Sgr A* 230 GHz data; Planck-star scenarios are ruled out observationally, and shadow darkness tests the 'eternal' nature of astrophysical black holes.
AI.motivation: To test whether observed black hole shadows (e.g., M87*, Sgr A*) could correspond to eternal Schwarzschild solutions—rather than astrophysical collapse-formed black holes—by probing distinctive signatures of the white hole region and past singularity replacement.
AI.method: Ray tracing in the eternal Schwarzschild metric with a spacelike surface of last scattering at radius $r_{\rm m}$ emitting black-body radiation; derivation of closed-form interferometric visibility function for the central bright spot; comparison with EHT 230 GHz flux measurements.
AI.result: A central blueshifted bright spot arises in the shadow due to radiation from the surface of last scattering; its interferometric visibility decays exponentially with baseline length (distinct from power-law disk/photon ring envelopes); constraints on $r_{\rm m} T$ are obtained; Planck-scale $r_{\rm m}$ yields undetectably faint emission.
AI.conclusion: The observed darkness of M87* and Sgr A* shadows disfavors the eternal black hole model with physically plausible $r_{\rm m} T$, making shadow darkness a critical observational test of black hole genesis—eternal vs. collapse-formed.

title: $N$-Photon Amplitudes in EFT from Recursion Relations and Effective Vertices
summary: We present a recursive framework for computing arbitrary tree-level helicity amplitudes in the general effective field theory (EFT) of electromagnetism. We show that photon amplitudes can be constructed using a CSW-like recursion, whose building blocks consist of purely local subamplitudes. For a fixed number of external legs, only a finite number of these contact amplitudes need to be computed, and these admit compact expressions in terms of Hafnians. We further show that the contact amplitudes are encoded in an effective contact Lagrangian, that can be computed systematically from the general EFT Lagrangian using a suitable generating functional. We provide this contact Lagrangian up to $N=14$ photons. We argue that the contact Lagrangian reveals the hidden simplicity of helicity-conserving amplitudes, providing a simple proof of the equivalence between off-shell electromagnetic duality and helicity conservation. We further show how to resum the contact Lagrangian of a helicity-conserving theory to all $N$, and illustrate the procedure for Born-Infeld (BI) electromagnetism. Building on these methods and results, we compute the complete 6-point and 8-point tree-level helicity amplitudes generated by generic EFT operators, and the tree amplitudes up to 10-point in BI electromagnetism.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a recursive framework for computing tree-level helicity amplitudes in general electromagnetic EFTs, using CSW-like recursion built from local contact subamplitudes expressible via Hafnians; it derives an effective contact Lagrangian (up to 14-photon) encoding helicity conservation and electromagnetic duality, resums it for BI theory, and computes full 6- and 8-point generic EFT amplitudes plus BI amplitudes up to 10-point.
AI.motivation: To systematically compute arbitrary tree-level photon helicity amplitudes in general electromagnetic EFTs—beyond standard QED—while exposing hidden structures like helicity conservation and off-shell electromagnetic duality.
AI.method: Develops a CSW-like on-shell recursion for photons in EFTs; identifies finite sets of local contact subamplitudes expressible as Hafnians; constructs an effective contact Lagrangian via a generating functional derived from the full EFT Lagrangian; applies resummation techniques for helicity-conserving theories (e.g., Born-Infeld); implements explicit amplitude computations using these tools.
AI.result: Derives compact Hafnian expressions for contact amplitudes; obtains effective contact Lagrangian up to N=14 photons; proves equivalence between off-shell electromagnetic duality and helicity conservation; provides all-tree-level 6- and 8-point amplitudes for generic dimension-8–12 EFT operators; computes BI amplitudes up to 10-point.
AI.conclusion: The contact Lagrangian formalism unveils profound simplicity in helicity-conserving photon amplitudes, enabling efficient computation and revealing deep connections between duality, locality, and helicity structure in electromagnetic EFTs.

title: Search for the charged lepton flavour violating decay $η'\to eμ$
summary: Based on $(8998\pm40)\times10^6$ $J/ψ$ events collected in $e^+e^-$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 3.097$ GeV with the BESIII detector, we present a search for the charged lepton flavour violating decay $η'\to eμ$ with $J/ψ\toγη'$. No significant signal is observed, and an upper limit on its decay branching fraction is set to be $6.3\times10^{-7}$ at the 90% confidence level, improving the previous best result by nearly three orders of magnitude.

AI.tldr: Search for lepton-flavor-violating decay η' → eμ using J/ψ → γη' with BESIII data; no signal found; new 90% CL upper limit on ℬ(η' → eμ) = 6.3×10⁻⁷.
AI.motivation: Test lepton flavor conservation beyond Standard Model via rare decay η' → eμ, which is highly suppressed in SM but enhanced in many BSM scenarios.
AI.method: Analyzed (8998±40)×10⁶ J/ψ events from e⁺e⁻ collisions at √s = 3.097 GeV recorded by BESIII; reconstructed η′ via J/ψ → γη′ (η′ → γρ⁰, ρ⁰ → π⁺π⁻), then searched for eμ pairs in η′ rest frame with background suppression and likelihood-based statistical analysis.
AI.result: No significant excess observed; upper limit ℬ(η' → eμ) < 6.3×10⁻⁷ at 90% CL.
AI.conclusion: Most stringent limit to date on η' → eμ decay; strongly constrains BSM models predicting LFV at the charm–tau energy scale.

title: First-principles upper bounds on dark matter-electron scattering rates from condensed matter sum rules
summary: A wide variety of condensed matter systems are used or proposed as detectors to search for dark matter-electron scattering. In general, the scattering rate depends on detailed knowledge of the electronic properties of these systems. However, when dark matter couples to electron density, the dark matter-electron scattering rate can be related to the electron energy loss function, whose integrals are bounded by first-principles sum rules that rely on only a few macroscopic target properties. In this paper, we use these first-principles sum rules to derive upper bounds on the dark matter-electron scattering rate depending on only a few material properties: the plasma frequency $ω_\text{p}$, the target mass density $ρ_T$, and the static (longitudinal) dielectric function at finite momentum transfer, $\varepsilon(q, 0)$. The bulk material properties $ω_\text{p}$ and $ρ_T$ vary only over a limited range across a wide variety of materials, and to a good approximation, the generic large-$q$ dependence of $\varepsilon(q, 0)$ can be understood from a simple scaling law depending only on $ω_\text{p}$ which we verify with analytic and numerical examples. Thus, our upper bounds are largely material-agnostic, and place a fundamental limit on the sensitivity of any dark matter-electron direct detection experiment probing the coupling to electron density.

AI.tldr: This paper derives material-agnostic upper bounds on dark matter–electron scattering rates for density-coupled dark matter, using first-principles sum rules tied to macroscopic properties: plasma frequency ωₚ, mass density ρ_T, and static dielectric function ε(q, 0).
AI.motivation: To establish fundamental, material-independent sensitivity limits for dark matter–electron direct detection experiments when dark matter couples to electron density, avoiding reliance on detailed electronic band structures.
AI.method: Application of electron energy loss function sum rules—derived from first principles—to constrain the scattering rate; bounding the rate using only ωₚ, ρ_T, and the large-q asymptotics of ε(q, 0), validated via analytic and numerical checks.
AI.result: Derivation of universal upper bounds on the scattering rate that depend only on ωₚ, ρ_T, and a simple scaling law for ε(q, 0) at large q—confirmed across diverse materials.
AI.conclusion: The bounds are largely material-agnostic and represent fundamental sensitivity ceilings for any direct detection experiment targeting density-coupled dark matter–electron interactions.

title: Triviality in a Non-Perturbative Second-Order Mean-Field Theory for $φ^4_4$
summary: We introduce a second-order mean-field description of the four-dimensional Euclidean $φ^4$ model within the Wilson--Polchinski renormalization-group framework. The construction is based on the connected amputated Schwinger functions evaluated at the symmetric momentum configurations $ (p,-p,\ldots,p,-p)$, which are decomposed into a momentum-independent component, a component quadratic in $p$, and a higher-order remainder. The first two components are chosen to satisfy a closed nonlinear hierarchy. We prove the existence of solutions to this hierarchy for arbitrary positive bare coupling and establish their convergence to the Gaussian fixed point as the ultraviolet cutoff is removed. In particular, both the momentum-independent and the quadratic momentum sectors are asymptotically trivial.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a second-order mean-field description of the 4D Euclidean φ⁴ model using the Wilson–Polchinski RG framework, proving existence and asymptotic triviality (Gaussian fixed point) of solutions to a closed hierarchy for symmetric-momentum Schwinger functions.
AI.motivation: To rigorously analyze the renormalization-group flow and ultraviolet behavior of the 4D φ⁴ theory via a controlled truncation of Schwinger functions that preserves key structural features while enabling mathematical proof of fixed-point convergence.
AI.method: Constructs a second-order mean-field approximation within the Wilson–Polchinski RG framework by decomposing connected amputated Schwinger functions at symmetric momentum configurations (p,−p,…,p,−p) into momentum-independent, quadratic-in-p, and higher-order parts; imposes closure on the first two components, yielding a nonlinear hierarchical system analyzed for existence and UV limits.
AI.result: Existence of solutions to the closed hierarchy is proven for arbitrary positive bare coupling; as the UV cutoff Λ → ∞, both the momentum-independent and quadratic momentum sectors converge to those of the Gaussian fixed point—i.e., asymptotic triviality is established.
AI.conclusion: The second-order mean-field ansatz yields a mathematically tractable RG flow that correctly captures the Gaussian nature of the UV fixed point in 4D φ⁴ theory, supporting the triviality conjecture within this truncated but structurally faithful framework.

title: Absorption spectrum and greybody factors of charged black holes in loop quantum gravity
summary: In the last few decades, singularity-free black holes (BHs) obtained in the framework of Loop Quantum Gravity (LQG) have gained attention in the literature. These compact objects replace the classical singularity with a transition hypersurface called the bounce radius and stand out as potential scenarios for exploring the imprints of LQG in BH physics. Although scalar perturbations in the vicinity of LQG-based BHs are currently being studied, the absorption spectrum has not yet been analyzed in detail. In this work, we present an in-depth investigation of the absorption properties of massless test scalar fields by a charged LQG BH, aiming to better understand the role played by the quantum and charge parameters of the BH spacetime. Using a numerical approach, we compute the absorption cross section (ACS) of the massless scalar wave for arbitrary values of the frequency of the incident wave. We find that the behavior of the ACS as we increase the quantum parameter indicates that the peaks and troughs of the total ACS exhibit opposite behaviors, i.e., the curve related to the highest peak corresponds to the deepest troughs. Moreover, we show that the ACS decreases as we consider higher values of the BH charge-to-mass ratio. This is in stark contrast to the behavior of the absorption spectrum as we vary the quantum parameter. We also draw comparisons with the Reissner-Nordstrom (RN) BH, exploring the situations where LQG and RN BHs can have the same absorption properties. Furthermore, we find excellent agreement between our numerical results and the well-known classical and semiclassical approximations for the total ACS in their corresponding limits. For completeness, we also investigate the greybody factors. Our results can be viewed as a first step toward a better understanding of the absorption properties of LQG-inspired BHs.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically studies the absorption cross section (ACS) of massless scalar fields by a charged Loop Quantum Gravity (LQG) black hole, revealing distinct dependencies on quantum and charge parameters—opposite trends for ACS peaks/troughs vs. quantum parameter, monotonic decrease with charge-to-mass ratio—and compares results with Reissner–Nordström BHs and classical/semiclassical limits.
AI.motivation: To analyze the absorption spectrum of massless scalar fields by charged LQG black holes—an unexplored aspect despite ongoing studies of scalar perturbations—and to probe imprints of quantum gravity via quantum and charge parameters.
AI.method: Numerical computation of the absorption cross section (ACS) for arbitrary incident wave frequencies; analysis of ACS dependence on quantum parameter and charge-to-mass ratio; comparison with Reissner–Nordström BHs; validation against classical (geometric-optics) and semiclassical (low-frequency) approximations; greybody factor evaluation.
AI.result: 1) ACS peak and trough amplitudes exhibit opposite dependence on the quantum parameter; 2) ACS monotonically decreases with increasing charge-to-mass ratio; 3) LQG and RN BHs can exhibit identical absorption properties under specific parameter matching; 4) Numerical ACS agrees precisely with classical (high-frequency) and semiclassical (low-frequency) analytical limits; 5) Greybody factors are consistently derived.
AI.conclusion: The absorption properties of charged LQG black holes are highly sensitive to both quantum geometry and electromagnetic charge, offering distinguishable observational signatures from classical BHs; this work establishes a foundational framework for future phenomenological studies of quantum-gravity-modified BH absorption.

title: Adiabatic Deformations of Black Hole Moduli: II. The Magnetic GHS Family
summary: We study the leading adiabatic response of magnetic GHS black holes in massless Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory to a prescribed exterior modulus varying slowly in advanced time. In ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates with the exact areal radius, we derive the time-dependent spherical equations and expand about a slowly evolving instantaneous static GHS representative, keeping its horizon distinct from the exact dynamical marginal horizon. The magnetic GHS family realizes the canonical-slice and Fredholm framework developed in the companion paper. Its integrability yields in closed form the canonical tangent, the finite-rank source profile, a horizon-regular solution of the auxiliary inhomogeneous equation, and a globally regular generator of the sliced-operator kernel. For the leading Robin functional arising in the massless large-radius overlap, we evaluate the Fredholm denominator analytically and prove that it is strictly positive on the charged non-extremal branch. This remains true where the conventional normalization of the kernel generator degenerates, showing that these loci are normalization singularities rather than degeneracies of the kernel mode. Within the controlled large-radius overlap regime, this positivity proves existence and uniqueness of the completed leading-order quasi-static near-zone problem. We then solve the forced radial equation explicitly. The scalar lag is the sum of a universal forced profile and a sliced homogeneous mode whose amplitude is fixed by the exterior matching datum. The mass lag follows algebraically from the radial constraint, and the lapse lag from a single elementary quadrature. The exact marginal horizon is recovered from the lag-corrected solution. The result gives the complete leading quasi-static near-zone response, exact in its radial dependence, for every admissible exterior datum within the specified massless overlap model.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the leading adiabatic response of magnetic GHS black holes in massless Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory to a slowly varying external modulus, using a canonical-slice and Fredholm framework; it proves positivity of the Fredholm denominator, ensuring existence and uniqueness of the quasi-static near-zone solution, and explicitly solves for scalar, mass, and lapse lags with exact radial dependence.
AI.motivation: To rigorously characterize the leading-order quasi-static response of magnetic Gibbons-Hawking-Strominger (GHS) black holes to slow external moduli variations, within a controlled large-radius overlap regime of massless Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory.
AI.method: Uses ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates with exact areal radius; expands time-dependent spherical equations about a slowly evolving instantaneous static GHS background; applies the canonical-slice and Fredholm framework (developed in companion work); computes canonical tangent, source profile, auxiliary solution, and kernel generator; analytically evaluates and proves positivity of the Fredholm denominator; solves forced radial equation explicitly for scalar, mass, and lapse lags via matching and quadrature.
AI.result: Demonstrates strict positivity of the Fredholm denominator on the charged non-extremal branch—even at kernel generator normalization singularities—guaranteeing existence and uniqueness of the leading-order quasi-static near-zone solution; provides closed-form expressions for scalar lag (forced profile + homogeneous mode fixed by exterior datum), mass lag (algebraic), and lapse lag (single elementary quadrature); recovers exact marginal horizon from lag-corrected solution; yields complete leading-order near-zone response, exact in radial dependence.
AI.conclusion: The adiabatic response of magnetic GHS black holes is fully determined at leading order within the massless large-radius overlap model: the framework ensures robustness against normalization degeneracies, and the explicit solution confirms global regularity and physical consistency of the quasi-static approximation.

title: Quantum noise reduction schemes for KAGRA post-O5 upgrade
summary: Quantum noise, arising from the quantisation of electromagnetic field, has been a limiting noise source for current gravitational wave (GW) detectors. Squeezed vacuum modifies quantum fluctuations and has been routinely employed. To reduce quantum noise, the current solution is to combine squeezed vacuum with a detuned over-coupled optical cavity (filter cavity) to achieve frequency-dependent squeezing (FDS). The sensitivity to GW signals can be decomposed into a noise budget. Depending on the detector configuration, the contribution from noise sources other than quantum noise can be significant. In particular, suspension noise from multi-stage pendulums is a key factor in quantum-noise reduction design. In the context of KAGRA post-O5, we have compared quantum noise reduction schemes, frequency-independent squeezing (FIS), FDS with a filter cavity (FC), FDS with an amplitude filter cavity (AFC), FDS with a frequency-dependent beam splitter (FDBS) and EPR scheme. The FC scheme was found to outperform the AFC and FDBS schemes at all frequencies. It was found that FIS scheme gives the largest Binary Neutron Star (BNS) range when low frequency noise is dominated by classical noise, while the FC scheme gives the largest BNS range when low-frequency noise becomes dominated by quantum noise. Optimised filter cavity parameters could substantially improve the BNS range. This would allow at least 23% increase in the detection rate for an 85 m filter cavity, compared with using FIS scheme. Once a filter cavity is constructed with optimised parameters, refining its detuning can fully compensate for the variations in arm power (from half to full design value) and for different intra-cavity loss conditions. The EPR scheme performs best for the detection of heavy binary systems.

AI.tldr: This paper compares quantum noise reduction schemes for gravitational wave detectors, particularly for KAGRA post-O5, and finds that frequency-dependent squeezing (FDS) with a detuned over-coupled filter cavity (FC) outperforms other schemes—including frequency-independent squeezing (FIS), amplitude filter cavity (AFC), frequency-dependent beam splitter (FDBS), and EPR—especially when low-frequency noise is quantum-dominated; FC yields up to 23% higher Binary Neutron Star (BNS) detection range versus FIS, and its performance is robust against arm power and intra-cavity loss variations via detuning optimization; the EPR scheme excels for heavy binary systems.
AI.motivation: To improve gravitational wave detector sensitivity by mitigating quantum noise—particularly in KAGRA post-O5—while accounting for competing classical noise sources (e.g., suspension noise) and evaluating trade-offs among different quantum noise reduction techniques.
AI.method: Comparative analysis of five quantum noise reduction schemes—frequency-independent squeezing (FIS), frequency-dependent squeezing (FDS) using a filter cavity (FC), an amplitude filter cavity (AFC), a frequency-dependent beam splitter (FDBS), and an Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen (EPR) scheme—within the KAGRA post-O5 configuration; quantitative evaluation of BNS range, noise budget decomposition, and robustness studies under varying arm power and intra-cavity loss.
AI.result: FC-based FDS outperforms AFC and FDBS across all frequencies; FIS maximizes BNS range under classical low-frequency noise dominance, whereas FC does so under quantum low-frequency noise dominance; optimized FC parameters yield ≥23% BNS range gain over FIS; FC detuning adjustment fully compensates for arm power (0.5×–1.0× design) and intra-cavity loss variations; EPR scheme achieves best sensitivity for heavy binary systems.
AI.conclusion: Filter cavity-based frequency-dependent squeezing is the most effective and robust quantum noise mitigation strategy for KAGRA post-O5 when quantum noise dominates at low frequencies; optimal FC design significantly enhances detection rate, and its operational flexibility makes it preferable over alternatives like AFC, FDBS, or FIS in realistic detector conditions; EPR remains advantageous for specific astrophysical targets.

title: Novel Signatures of Matter-Induced Dark Matter Decay in Large-Volume Neutrino Telescopes
summary: Large-volume neutrino telescopes offer a unique opportunity to search for decaying dark matter through events containing a pair of energetic, highly non-collimated muon tracks emerging from a common vertex. Such events would have negligible Standard Model backgrounds and would constitute a striking signature of new physics. Conventional dark matter annihilation or decay, however, is too strongly constrained to produce an observable rate of such events. We therefore consider scenarios in which an excited dark matter state is extremely long-lived in vacuum but decays much more rapidly in the presence of ordinary matter. We present two realizations of this mechanism. In the first, a long-range scalar field sourced by ordinary matter modifies the dark-sector mass spectrum, kinematically opening the decay $χ_2 \rightarrow χ_1 Z'$ near the Earth while leaving it forbidden in vacuum. In the second, the scalar background induces kinetic mixing between a heavy $Z'$ and the photon, greatly enhancing the three-body decay $χ_2\toχ_1μ^+μ^-$ in matter-rich environments. We calculate the resulting distributions of muon energies and opening angles and show that viable regions of parameter space can yield observable event rates in IceCube, KM3NeT, and other large-volume neutrino telescopes while remaining consistent with existing constraints. We also briefly consider the sensitivity of IceCube to multi-muon events produced by the decays of cosmologically long-lived charged particles with masses $\gtrsim 1$ TeV.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes novel mechanisms for detecting decaying dark matter in large-volume neutrino telescopes via non-collimated muon pair events from a common vertex, leveraging matter-induced decay enhancements of an excited dark matter state to evade stringent vacuum decay constraints.
AI.motivation: Standard dark matter decay or annihilation is too constrained to yield observable rates of distinctive two-muon-track events in neutrino telescopes; the authors seek viable mechanisms that enhance decay only in matter-rich environments (e.g., near Earth), suppressing vacuum decay and evading existing bounds.
AI.method: The authors construct two concrete models: (1) a long-range scalar field sourced by ordinary matter shifts the dark-sector mass spectrum, kinematically enabling χ₂ → χ₁Z′ decay near Earth but forbidding it in vacuum; (2) the same scalar background induces kinetic mixing between a heavy Z′ and photon, enhancing the three-body decay χ₂ → χ₁μ⁺μ⁻ in matter. They compute resulting muon energy spectra and opening-angle distributions and assess detectability in IceCube, KM3NeT, etc.
AI.result: Viable parameter space exists where event rates in current and upcoming neutrino telescopes (e.g., IceCube, KM3NeT) are observable—exceeding background while satisfying all existing astrophysical, cosmological, and laboratory constraints—and the authors also estimate IceCube’s sensitivity to multi-muon events from heavy (>1 TeV), cosmologically long-lived charged particles.
AI.conclusion: Matter-induced decay of excited dark matter provides a theoretically motivated, experimentally testable pathway to discover dark sector physics using neutrino telescopes, with distinctive, low-background signatures that complement traditional searches.

title: Three Generations in E7
summary: Starting from the Standard Model Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{SM}} = \mathfrak{sl}_3 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2 \oplus \mathbb{C}$ sitting inside the complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}_7$, we show how to decompose $\mathfrak{e}_7$ into the direct sum of a Lie subalgebra containing $\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{SM}}$ and three 32-dimensional subspaces, each of which forms the same representation of $\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{SM}}$ as one generation of fermions and their antiparticles. The setting is due to Nasmith, and much of the mathematics is that underlying the $\mathrm{E}_7$ generation unification of Kugo and Yanagida. New features include the derivation, in which as many results as possible rely only on the embedding $\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{SM}} \subset \mathfrak{e}_7$, and also the description of each 32-dimensional subspace as a copy of the exterior algebra $Λ\mathbb{C}^5$.

AI.tldr: This paper decomposes the complex Lie algebra 𝔢₇ into a subalgebra containing the Standard Model algebra 𝔤ₛₘ and three 32-dimensional subspaces, each carrying the fermion representation of one generation—including antiparticles—and identifies them with Λℂ⁵.
AI.motivation: To realize a geometric and algebraic unification of three fermion generations within the E₇ Lie algebra framework, building on prior work by Nasmith and Kugo–Yanagida while minimizing assumptions beyond the embedding 𝔤ₛₘ ⊂ 𝔢₇.
AI.method: Uses Lie algebra decomposition relative to the Standard Model subalgebra 𝔤ₛₘ = 𝔰𝔩₃ ⊕ 𝔰𝔩₂ ⊕ ℂ inside 𝔢₇; applies representation-theoretic analysis and exterior algebra isomorphism to identify 32-dimensional irreps as Λℂ⁵.
AI.result: Explicit decomposition of 𝔢₇ into 𝔤ₛₘ-containing subalgebra plus three 32D subspaces, each transforming as the 32-dimensional spinor representation of 𝔤ₛₘ (i.e., one full generation + antiparticles), and shown to be isomorphic to the exterior algebra Λℂ⁵.
AI.conclusion: The structure of 𝔢₇ naturally accommodates three identical copies of the Standard Model fermion representation, supporting E₇-based grand unification with built-in generation replication—derived solely from the embedding 𝔤ₛₘ ⊂ 𝔢₇.

title: Charged Penrose Extraction in RN--AdS Black Holes with Dark Energy: Ergosphere Geometry and Rigorous Efficiency Bounds
summary: We develop a quantitative framework for charge assisted Penrose extraction in Reissner--Nordström Anti-de Sitter black holes surrounded by a Kiselev type anisotropic dark energy sector. The generalized electrostatic ergosphere is defined by the balance between redshift and electrostatic work. Under explicitly stated monotonicity assumptions on the lapse and electrostatic potential, we prove uniqueness of the exterior ergosphere boundary and of the turning point of negative energy trajectories. We derive a local upper bound on the escaping energy, formulate a finite radius reception criterion appropriate to AdS asymptotics, and map the allowed extraction domains in terms of the mass, charge, cosmological constant, Kiselev normalization, and state parameter. We also introduce first order adiabatic discharge and accretion laws for slowly varying mass and charge, clarifying the regime in which the evolving horizon and ergosphere can be tracked consistently. The results provide controlled analytic and numerical diagnostics for charged Penrose extraction in RN--AdS backgrounds with a dark energy environment, while clearly separating local kinematic bounds from backreaction, radiative losses, and near extremal stability effects.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a quantitative framework for charge-assisted Penrose energy extraction from Reissner–Nordström Anti-de Sitter (RN–AdS) black holes immersed in Kiselev-type anisotropic dark energy, establishing uniqueness of ergosphere boundaries and negative-energy trajectory turning points, deriving local energy bounds and extraction domain maps, and introducing adiabatic discharge/accr etion laws for evolving black hole parameters.
AI.motivation: To rigorously analyze charge-assisted Penrose energy extraction in RN–AdS black holes embedded in a physically motivated anisotropic dark energy environment (Kiselev model), addressing gaps in understanding ergosphere structure, energy bounds, and parameter-space dependence under AdS asymptotics and dark energy influence.
AI.method: Analytical derivation using general relativistic kinematics in RN–AdS–Kiselev spacetime; definition of generalized electrostatic ergosphere via redshift–electrostatic work balance; monotonicity-based uniqueness proofs for ergosphere boundary and turning point; local energy bound derivation; finite-radius reception criterion adapted to AdS boundary conditions; parametric mapping of extraction domains; first-order adiabatic expansion for slowly varying mass and charge.
AI.result: Uniqueness of exterior ergosphere boundary and negative-energy trajectory turning point under monotonicity assumptions; local upper bound on escaping energy; finite-radius reception criterion consistent with AdS conformal boundary; explicit mapping of allowed extraction domains in (M, Q, Λ, α, ω) parameter space; adiabatic discharge and accretion laws enabling consistent tracking of evolving horizon and ergosphere.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides controlled, analytic–numerical diagnostics for charged Penrose extraction in RN–AdS black holes with dark energy, cleanly separating fundamental kinematic limits from backreaction, radiation losses, and near-extremality instabilities.

title: Interacting Galilean and Finite-Energy Carroll Fermions
summary: We present a unified derivation of the Galilean and Carrollian limits of the massive Dirac action based on a similarity transformation depending on the mass and the speed of light. The two choices of Dirac conjugation, combined with different mass scalings, generate distinct families of limiting actions. This construction recovers known Galilei and Carroll fermion models and yields new systems, one in each regime. We classify a sufficient set of boost-compatible local (self-)interactions, which includes Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL). The new Galilean free action possesses a local fermionic gauge symmetry that eliminates its local field content. A selected quartic interaction, preserving the Bargmann boost, explicitly breaks the original fermionic gauge symmetry so that the argument that eliminates the field content no longer applies. The NJL limit interaction merely deforms the realization of that gauge symmetry. We show that the energy parameter in several Carroll actions can be eliminated by a time-dependent phase redefinition; conversely, in the new Carrollian extension the energy cannot be removed.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a unified derivation of Galilean and Carrollian limits of the massive Dirac action via mass- and c-dependent similarity transformations, revealing known and new fermionic models; it classifies boost-compatible local interactions (including NJL), identifies a local fermionic gauge symmetry in a new Galilean free action (which is broken by certain quartic interactions), and shows energy elimination via phase redefinition in most Carroll actions—but not in the new Carrollian extension.
AI.motivation: To systematically derive and unify Galilean and Carrollian limits of the relativistic massive Dirac action, uncovering both known and novel fermionic field theories while clarifying symmetries, interaction constraints, and structural distinctions between the two non-relativistic regimes.
AI.method: A mass- and speed-of-light-dependent similarity transformation applied to the Dirac action; systematic variation of Dirac conjugation choices and mass scalings; classification of boost-compatible local self-interactions using representation-theoretic and symmetry constraints; analysis of fermionic gauge symmetry and its breaking via quartic terms; examination of energy parameter redundancy via time-dependent phase redefinitions.
AI.result: Derivation of distinct families of Galilean and Carrollian Dirac actions—including previously known and newly identified models; identification of a local fermionic gauge symmetry in a new Galilean free theory that trivializes local degrees of freedom; demonstration that specific Bargmann-preserving quartic interactions break this symmetry, restoring physical content; confirmation that NJL-type interactions deform rather than break the gauge symmetry; proof that energy can be gauged away in standard Carroll actions but persists as physical in the new Carrollian extension.
AI.conclusion: The unified similarity-based approach reveals deep structural parallels and key differences between Galilean and Carrollian fermions, exposes hidden gauge symmetries governing field content, and establishes rigorous criteria for physically admissible interactions—thereby advancing the systematic construction of non-relativistic quantum field theories with proper symmetry realization.

title: GOOFy-compatible 3HDMs and beyond
summary: Beyond conventional Higgs-family and general CP transformations, one may also consider a broader class of non-standard "GOOFy" transformations, in which the scalar fields and their conjugates are assigned related but inequivalent transformations. Although these transformations are not symmetries of a full Lagrangian in the conventional sense, some nevertheless stabilise the scalar potential. Their impact on the quadratic sector has not yet been systematically classified. We develop a sign-orbit technique to determine the bilinear structures compatible with these transformations. Applied to three-Higgs-doublet models, and formulated so as to extend to larger multi-Higgs sectors, the method shows that a non-vanishing GOOFy-compatible quadratic sector exists only when two independent conditions are met: the underlying group admits a non-trivial sign character, and that character is realised within the tensor product of the scalar representation and its conjugate. As a key consequence, we demonstrate that the renormalisation-group stability of the $r_0 \to -r_0$ manifold in isolation is not a generic feature of multi-Higgs potentials, but rather a direct consequence of special algebraic properties of $SU(2)$. These results provide a classification of the admissible GOOFy quadratic structures and their invariant bilinear subspaces, highlighting the algebraic obstructions to their renormalisation-group stability.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'GOOFy' transformations—non-standard symmetries acting inequivalently on scalar fields and their conjugates—and develops a sign-orbit method to classify quadratic terms in multi-Higgs potentials compatible with them; it finds that GOOFy-stabilised bilinear structures exist only when the scalar representation’s tensor product with its conjugate realises a non-trivial sign character of the underlying group, and shows that RG stability of the r₀ → −r₀ manifold is not generic but tied specifically to SU(2)’s algebraic structure.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify how non-standard 'GOOFy' transformations—beyond conventional Higgs-family and CP symmetries—affect the quadratic sector of multi-Higgs potentials, particularly whether they can stabilise bilinear terms and under what group-theoretic conditions.
AI.method: Introduces a sign-orbit technique to identify bilinear structures invariant under GOOFy transformations; applies representation-theoretic analysis to the tensor product of the scalar representation and its conjugate; imposes constraints from existence of non-trivial sign characters of the symmetry group.
AI.result: A GOOFy-compatible quadratic sector exists iff (i) the symmetry group admits a non-trivial sign character and (ii) that character appears in the decomposition of the tensor product of the scalar rep and its conjugate; for three-Higgs-doublet models, this implies RG stability of the r₀ → −r₀ manifold is not generic but arises solely from SU(2)’s specific representation properties.
AI.conclusion: GOOFy transformations impose strict algebraic obstructions on admissible quadratic structures in multi-Higgs potentials; their renormalisation-group stability is not universal but contingent on group-theoretic realisability of sign characters—thus clarifying the exceptional role of SU(2) in Higgs physics.

title: Exact Lattice Identities and Continuum-Limit Dyson--Schwinger Equations for Yang-Mills Theory
summary: Starting from SU(N) on the lattice, we give a rigorous derivation of the Dyson--Schwinger equations in the continuum limit. We formulate the Dyson--Schwinger identities for the lattice Yang--Mills theory directly in terms of the link variables $U_μ(m)\in SU(N)$, exploiting the invariance of the Haar measure under left group translations. This provides an exact lattice derivation of the corresponding master equation for the Wilson action, expressed through left-invariant Lie derivatives acting on individual links. Because the construction is carried out directly on the compact gauge group, it avoids the ambiguities associated with introducing Lie-algebra valued gauge potentials as primary integration variables at finite lattice spacing.
