For practical applications, in a second part we then break down the gauge degree of freedom by choosing Feynman gauge. We analyze the continuum-limit form of the resulting lattice identities and derive equations for the one- and two-point connected functions. Under a further simplifying reduction, these equations close to a tractable scalar system. Our results establish a direct bridge between exact lattice identities and the functional equations commonly used in continuum nonperturbative studies of Yang--Mills theory.

AI.tldr: Rigorous lattice derivation of Dyson-Schwinger equations for SU(N) Yang-Mills theory using Haar-measure-invariant link variables, avoiding Lie-algebra ambiguities; yields continuum-limit functional equations for connected correlators.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous, ambiguity-free derivation of Dyson-Schwinger equations directly from the lattice formulation of SU(N) Yang-Mills theory, circumventing issues arising from premature introduction of Lie-algebra-valued gauge potentials at finite lattice spacing.
AI.method: Formulating Dyson-Schwinger identities on the lattice using SU(N)-valued link variables and left-invariant Lie derivatives acting on links, leveraging Haar measure invariance under left group translations; subsequently fixing Feynman gauge and taking the continuum limit to derive equations for one- and two-point connected functions.
AI.result: Exact lattice master equation for the Wilson action in terms of left-invariant Lie derivatives; continuum-limit Dyson-Schwinger equations for connected correlators; reduction to a tractable scalar system under simplifying assumptions.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a mathematically sound, direct connection between exact lattice identities and continuum functional methods in nonperturbative Yang-Mills theory, validating and grounding standard continuum approaches in first-principles lattice QCD.

title: Kinematic Bounds on Charged Energy Extraction in the Purely Electric Branch of Euler--Heisenberg Type f(R,T) Black Holes
summary: We derive and test kinematic upper bounds on charged energy extraction in the purely electric branch of a static $f(R,T)$ black hole family sourced by an Euler--Heisenberg type nonlinear electromagnetic sector. The analysis is restricted to external, minimally coupled probe particles on the fixed background. In this electric solution the field remains Coulombic up to an additive gauge constant; the nonlinear electromagnetic and matter-coupling coefficients therefore affect extraction indirectly through the metric, the event-horizon position, and the global causal structure. We obtain a general local bound retaining nonzero angular momentum and radial velocity of the negative energy fragment, and identify the commonly used zero angular momentum turning-point choice as an upper envelope rather than a generic decay configuration. A co-moving split supplies a locally four momentum-conserving benchmark. We classify horizons with the double root conditions $\mathcal F=\mathcal F'=0$, distinguish asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter branches, and impose the corresponding global outward-accessibility criterion. In the de Sitter static patch the electrostatic energy is referenced to the cosmological horizon, so the relevant scale is $Q(1/r_+-1/r_c)$ rather than $Q/r_+$. Reproducible scans compare Reissner--Nordström, Einstein--Euler--Heisenberg type, $f(R,T)$--Maxwell, and full $f(R,T)$--Euler--Heisenberg type backgrounds. The results show that the branch-referenced horizon potential controls the local upper envelope, whereas the asymptotic structure determines whether an outward trajectory can reach infinity, a cosmological horizon, or only a finite outer turning point.

AI.tldr: This paper derives kinematic upper bounds on charged energy extraction from a static f(R,T) black hole with Euler-Heisenberg nonlinear electrodynamics, analyzing probe particle dynamics in fixed backgrounds and showing that horizon potential sets local extraction limits while global causal structure (asymptotics) governs accessibility of outward trajectories.
AI.motivation: To extend charged energy extraction analysis beyond standard Reissner–Nordström black holes to more general gravitational and electromagnetic frameworks—specifically static f(R,T) gravity coupled to Euler–Heisenberg nonlinear electrodynamics—and clarify the roles of horizon geometry and asymptotic structure in setting physical limits on energy extraction.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of kinematic upper bounds for charged energy extraction using geodesic motion of minimally coupled test particles in fixed f(R,T) black hole backgrounds; classification of horizons via double-root conditions (F = F' = 0); distinction of asymptotically flat, dS, and AdS branches; comparison across four background types via reproducible parameter scans; use of co-moving split for four-momentum-conserving benchmark and identification of zero-angular-momentum turning point as an upper envelope.
AI.result: The local upper bound on charged energy extraction is governed by the branch-referenced horizon electrostatic potential (e.g., Q(1/r₊ − 1/r_c) in dS), not just Q/r₊; the zero-angular-momentum turning-point configuration yields an upper envelope—not generic decay—while co-moving splits provide momentum-conserving benchmarks; global outward accessibility depends critically on asymptotic structure (flat vs. dS vs. AdS).
AI.conclusion: Charged energy extraction efficiency is locally capped by horizon-scale electrostatic potential modulated by f(R,T) and nonlinear EM parameters via metric deformation, but globally constrained by causal structure: only asymptotically flat or dS backgrounds permit unbounded outward trajectories (to infinity or cosmological horizon), whereas AdS-like or finite-turning-point geometries limit extraction range.

title: Beyond Borel Windows: A Systematic Optimization Framework for QCD Sum Rules
comment: 13 pages and 5 figures. Presented at the 29th High-Energy Physics International Conference in QCD (QCD26), Montpellier, France
summary: We propose a systematic optimization framework for determining the sum rule window in QCD Laplace sum rules. Instead of relying primarily on fixed convergence percentages and visual plateau selection, the procedure combines an OPE entropy criterion, local mass stationarity, and a correlated analysis of the Laplace parameter $τ$, the continuum threshold $t_c$, and the interpolating-current mixing angle $θ$. The normalized OPE entropy is introduced to quantify the redistribution of the QCD contributions between the perturbative and nonperturbative sectors and to delimit an initial Working Region. This domain is subsequently refined by minimizing the residual variation of the mass estimator and requiring weak sensitivity to the continuum threshold and to the current composition. As an application, we study the lowest fully charmed tetraquark state with quantum numbers $J^{PC}=2^{++}$ using a mixed diquark--antidiquark and meson--meson interpolating current. The optimization selects $θ=17.2^\circ\pm0.4^\circ$, $\sqrt{t_c}=7.08\pm0.08~\mathrm{GeV}$, and $τ=0.410\pm0.010~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$, leading to the mass prediction $M_{c\bar c c\bar c}^{2^{++}}=(6.32\pm0.11)~\mathrm{GeV}$. The predicted state lies in the near-threshold region of the di-$J/ψ$ spectrum and is compatible, within uncertainties, with the lowest resonant component reported by ATLAS and with the enhancement parametrized as $BW_0$ in the recent CMS publication. The proposed framework provides a reproducible way of identifying finite domains of reduced auxiliary-parameter sensitivity and of incorporating the remaining dependence into the final uncertainty.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a systematic optimization framework for QCD Laplace sum rules to objectively determine the sum rule window, using OPE entropy, mass stationarity, and correlated analysis of τ, t_c, and θ; applied to the 2^{++} fully charmed tetraquark, it predicts M = 6.32 ± 0.11 GeV, consistent with ATLAS and CMS near-threshold observations.
AI.motivation: To overcome subjectivity in traditional Laplace sum rule analyses—particularly arbitrary plateau selection and fixed OPE convergence thresholds—by establishing a reproducible, quantitative, and correlated optimization of auxiliary parameters (τ, t_c, θ).
AI.method: Introduces normalized OPE entropy to define an initial Working Region; refines it by minimizing residual mass variation and enforcing weak sensitivity to t_c and θ; performs correlated Bayesian-like uncertainty propagation across τ, t_c, and θ using stationarity and entropy constraints.
AI.result: Optimized parameters: θ = 17.2° ± 0.4°, √t_c = 7.08 ± 0.08 GeV, τ = 0.410 ± 0.010 GeV⁻²; yields mass prediction M_{c\bar{c}c\bar{c}}^{2^{++}} = 6.32 ± 0.11 GeV, consistent with near-threshold di-J/ψ structures observed by ATLAS and CMS.
AI.conclusion: The framework replaces ad hoc choices with objective, entropy- and stationarity-driven criteria, enabling robust, uncertainty-aware extraction of hadron masses from QCD sum rules, particularly for exotic multiquark states.

title: Scalar Hair at the String-Black-Hole Correspondence
summary: We study static, spherically symmetric axion--dilaton solutions of the tree-level four-dimensional string effective action. Using the sigma-model structure of the scalar sector, we show that the full family of static, spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat solutions is obtained as the $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ orbit of the pure-dilaton FJNW solution, and we characterize the associated axion--dilaton charge space. We then analyze the perturbative regime of these solutions by comparing the onset of $α'$ curvature corrections with that of string-loop corrections. Finally, we apply the string--black-hole correspondence criterion to the FJNW family by evaluating the local $α'$ curvature diagnostic at the physical size $R_{\rm typ}$ of a highly excited string state. With the normalization fixed on the Schwarzschild branch, Schwarzschild saturates the nominal $α'$ threshold at the correspondence surface, whereas every scalar-haired FJNW branch lies above it. More generally, independently of the common overall normalization within the matching prescription, every nonzero-hair branch has a larger curvature diagnostic at the correspondence surface than Schwarzschild. Away from the correspondence point, scalar-haired exteriors may remain under $α'$ control at sufficiently weak local self-gravity and may provide perturbatively controlled long-distance fields of highly excited string states whenever the local string coupling also remains weak.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes static, spherically symmetric axion–dilaton black hole solutions in 4D string effective theory, showing they form an SL(2,R) orbit of the FJNW dilaton solution; it compares α′ and loop corrections, and applies the string–black-hole correspondence criterion—finding that scalar-hair branches generically exceed Schwarzschild’s α′ curvature threshold at the correspondence surface, though may remain perturbatively controlled at weak coupling and gravity.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify and assess the physical viability of static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat axion–dilaton black hole solutions in tree-level 4D string effective theory, particularly in light of stringy corrections (α′ and gₛ) and the string–black-hole correspondence.
AI.method: Exploits the SL(2,R) sigma-model symmetry of the axion–dilaton sector to generate the full solution family from the pure-dilaton FJNW seed; computes and compares scales of α′ curvature and string-loop corrections; evaluates the local α′ curvature diagnostic R_typ²R at the typical size R_typ of a highly excited string state, using the string–black-hole correspondence criterion.
AI.result: The full solution space is the SL(2,R) orbit of the FJNW solution; nonzero axion–dilaton hair increases the α′ curvature diagnostic at the correspondence surface relative to Schwarzschild—regardless of overall normalization—implying scalar-hair branches lie deeper in the α′-strong regime there; however, away from correspondence, some scalar-hair exteriors can remain perturbatively valid if both local curvature and string coupling are sufficiently weak.
AI.conclusion: While Schwarzschild saturates the nominal α′ threshold at the string–black-hole correspondence surface, all nonzero-hair FJNW branches exceed it—suggesting scalar hair is disfavored at correspondence; yet, such hairy solutions may still serve as perturbatively controlled long-distance descriptions of highly excited strings in regimes of weak local self-gravity and weak string coupling.

title: Constructing the canonical harmonic coordinates of Kerr metric to the fourth post-Minkowskian order
summary: In this paper we construct the canonical harmonic coordinates of the Kerr metric within the multipolar post-Minkowskian (MPM) formalism to the fourth post-Minkowskian (4PM) order. Based on the well known Geroch--Hansen moments of Kerr metric and Gürsel's theorem, we derive the exact canonical MPM moments $\mathrm{M}_L,\mathrm{S}_L$, which are free of any gauge moments. With these moments, we iteratively compute the gothic metric perturbation $h^{μν}_{\mathrm{can}}$ up to 4PM order and compute the 4PM canonical metric $g_{μν}^{\mathrm{can}}$. The resulting spatial and time components of these metrics are even functions of the spin parameter $a$ while the mixed components are odd. This parity property distinguishes the canonical coordinates from other harmonic coordinates. To contrast this minimal-gauge construction, we also extract the 1PM source moments of the Kerr metric in the Jiang--Lin coordinates. We find that the Jiang--Lin representation possesses non-vanishing gauge moments starting from the 1PM order, whereas in the canonical representation gauge moments vanish to all orders. This comparison highlights the canonical coordinates as the most gauge-pure representation of the Kerr metric in the MPM framework. The complete canonical metric for the Schwarzschild case is also computed to all PM orders. A recent independent construction by Damgaard et al. using momentum-space recursion yields 4PM equivalent results expressed as a power series in $a$, providing a cross-validation of our closed-form 4PM canonical metric. The coordinate transformation linking the canonical Kerr coordinates to previously known harmonic Kerr coordinates remains an open problem.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the canonical harmonic coordinates for the Kerr metric within the multipolar post-Minkowskian (MPM) formalism up to 4PM order, deriving gauge-free canonical moments and metric components with definite parity in spin; it contrasts this minimal-gauge representation with Jiang–Lin coordinates (which contain gauge moments from 1PM), confirms consistency with independent momentum-space results, and provides the all-order canonical Schwarzschild metric.
AI.motivation: To obtain a gauge-pure, canonical harmonic representation of the Kerr metric in the MPM framework—free of spurious gauge moments—and establish its uniqueness and physical interpretability via parity properties and moment structure.
AI.method: Uses Geroch–Hansen multipole moments and Gürsel's theorem to derive exact canonical MPM mass and current moments (M_L, S_L); iteratively solves the vacuum Einstein equations in harmonic gauge to compute the gothic metric perturbation h^{μν}_can and canonical metric g_{μν}^can up to 4PM; analyzes parity under spin inversion; compares with Jiang–Lin coordinates by extracting their source moments; cross-validates against Damgaard et al.'s momentum-space 4PM result.
AI.result: Explicit 4PM canonical Kerr metric g_{μν}^can in harmonic coordinates where spatial/time components are even and mixed components odd in spin parameter a; vanishing gauge moments at all orders in canonical representation versus non-vanishing ones from 1PM in Jiang–Lin; complete all-PM canonical Schwarzschild metric; closed-form 4PM metric validated against independent momentum-space series expansion.
AI.conclusion: The canonical harmonic coordinates provide the most gauge-pure MPM representation of Kerr, uniquely characterized by gauge-free moments and spin-parity symmetry; they serve as a fundamental reference for gravitational-wave modeling and theoretical studies of black hole geometry in the PM expansion.

title: Surviving correlations across a horizon: reflected entropy for bosonic fields in non-inertial frames and black hole spacetimes
summary: We study the reflected entropy and the Markov gap for modes of a free bosonic field shared by inertial observers (Alice, Charlie) and a uniformly accelerated one (Bob), for a bipartite Bell state and the tripartite Werner (W) and Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states. The bosonic Bogoliubov transformation spans an infinite-dimensional Fock space with an unbounded squeezing parameter unlike the fermionic case. By identifying a conserved charge, we block-diagonalize the reduced density matrices into exact two-dimensional sectors, yielding closed or semi-analytic forms for all three states. Although bosonic entanglement is known to vanish asymptotically, the Alice--Bob reflected entropy instead saturates at a nonzero saturation floor, retaining the surviving classical correlation, and converges to the value Alice shares with Bob's causally disconnected partner. Crucially, only the inter-wedge reflected entropy diverges, linearly in the squeezing parameter---the sharp distinction from the fermionic case, where it stays bounded---while the Markov gaps saturate. The construction transfers verbatim to a Schwarzschild black hole, where the saturation values become mass-independent constants.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes reflected entropy and Markov gap for free bosonic field modes shared among inertial and uniformly accelerated observers, using exact block-diagonalization via a conserved charge; it finds bosonic reflected entropy saturates (unlike fermions) and inter-wedge reflected entropy diverges linearly with squeezing—key distinctions from fermionic analogs—and extends results to Schwarzschild black holes.
AI.motivation: To resolve how bosonic entanglement structure—particularly reflected entropy and Markov gap—behaves under acceleration (Unruh effect) and in curved spacetime, contrasting with known fermionic behavior where entanglement measures remain bounded.
AI.method: Exact diagonalization of reduced density matrices by identifying a conserved charge, enabling block-diagonalization into two-dimensional sectors; application of bosonic Bogoliubov transformation with unbounded squeezing parameter; evaluation of reflected entropy and Markov gap for Bell, Werner (W), and GHZ states across inertial–accelerated observer configurations.
AI.result: Alice–Bob reflected entropy saturates at a nonzero floor (preserving classical correlation), while inter-wedge reflected entropy diverges linearly in squeezing—unlike fermions where it remains bounded; Markov gaps saturate; all saturation values become mass-independent constants in the Schwarzschild black hole limit.
AI.conclusion: Bosonic field entanglement exhibits qualitatively distinct nonlocal correlation structure under acceleration: reflected entropy retains classical correlations asymptotically and diverges in inter-wedge geometry, revealing a fundamental difference from fermionic fields and providing robust, mass-independent signatures in black hole physics.

title: Photon-nucleon entanglement in Compton scattering at low and high energies
summary: We study spin-spin entanglement in the final state photon-nucleon system in Compton scattering, both at low energy below the pion threshold and at high energy in perturbative QCD to next-to-leading order. We first establish a no-go theorem showing that, for any spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ target, entanglement cannot be generated in unpolarized Compton scattering if the scattering amplitudes are real. We then consider polarized Compton scattering off the electron, the proton and the neutron. At low energy, we uncover a rich variety of maximally entangled Bell states and their unitary equivalents realized across different regions of the kinematic plane. Interestingly, the proton and neutron targets exhibit distinct patterns of entanglement. In the neutron case, the electric and magnetic polarizabilities dramatically influence the pattern and even the existence of entanglement. This suggests that entanglement can serve as a novel tool for investigating the detailed electromagnetic properties of the nucleons.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates spin-spin entanglement in photon-nucleon Compton scattering across low- and high-energy regimes, proves a no-go theorem for entanglement generation in unpolarized scattering with real amplitudes, identifies maximally entangled Bell states in polarized scattering off e⁻, p, n, and reveals that neutron polarizabilities critically control entanglement presence and structure—proposing entanglement as a probe of nucleon electromagnetic structure.
AI.motivation: To explore whether and how spin-spin entanglement arises in Compton scattering as a function of target type (e⁻, p, n), polarization, energy regime, and fundamental scattering amplitudes; and to assess its potential as a novel probe of nucleon structure (e.g., polarizabilities).
AI.method: Analytical quantum information analysis of spin density matrices derived from Compton scattering amplitudes; derivation of a no-go theorem for entanglement under reality condition on amplitudes; explicit computation of concurrence and Bell-state classification across the kinematic plane at low energy (chiral effective theory / empirical amplitudes) and high energy (pQCD NLO).
AI.result: 1) No entanglement is possible in unpolarized Compton scattering off spin-½ targets if amplitudes are real. 2) Polarized scattering yields maximal entanglement (Bell states or unitary equivalents) over broad kinematic regions. 3) Proton and neutron show qualitatively distinct entanglement patterns. 4) Neutron entanglement is highly sensitive to electric (αₙ) and magnetic (βₙ) polarizabilities—altering both pattern and existence of entanglement.
AI.conclusion: Spin entanglement in Compton scattering is a viable, theoretically robust, and structurally informative observable: it discriminates between nucleons, encodes their electromagnetic polarizabilities, and offers a new quantum-informational lens into hadronic structure beyond conventional cross sections or asymmetries.

title: Partition Functions of Hermitian and PT-Symmetric Oscillators from Integrable Models
summary: We develop an ODE/IM-based formulation for the thermal partition function and the spectral zeta function of the homogeneous Hermitian and PT-symmetric oscillators. For both classes of systems, the quantization condition can be expressed using the counting function $a(E)$, which can be solved via the Destri-de Vega equation of the integrable model. We then express the partition function and spectral zeta function as contour integrals involving the counting function, thereby providing a direct bridge between quantum spectral functions and integrable models.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a connection between quantum spectral functions (thermal partition function and spectral zeta function) of Hermitian and PT-symmetric oscillators and integrable models via an ODE/IM formulation using the Destri-de Vega equation.
AI.motivation: To unify the treatment of spectral functions for Hermitian and PT-symmetric quantum oscillators by leveraging integrability through the ODE/IM correspondence.
AI.method: Uses the ODE/Integrable Model (ODE/IM) correspondence; formulates quantization via the counting function $a(E)$ solved with the Destri-de Vega equation; expresses partition and spectral zeta functions as contour integrals of $a(E)$.
AI.result: Derives contour integral representations of the thermal partition function and spectral zeta function in terms of the counting function $a(E)$, valid for both Hermitian and PT-symmetric homogeneous oscillators.
AI.conclusion: Provides a direct analytical bridge between quantum spectral data and integrable model structures, extending the ODE/IM framework to spectral zeta functions and thermal partition functions.

title: How Loud Must a Neutron-Star Merger Be to Reveal Its Equation of State?
summary: The tidal response of neutron stars during binary inspiral encodes the equation of state (EOS) of dense matter in the gravitational-wave signal. Quantifying the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) required to distinguish competing EOS models with third-generation detectors is therefore essential. We perform Bayesian nested-sampling parameter estimation on simulated binary neutron star signals observed by an Einstein Telescope plus two Cosmic Explorer detector network and compute the evidence difference between correct- and incorrect-EOS recovery models over a broad range of SNR. Across two tidal-deformability contrasts, a swap of the true and recovery EOS, and two binary mass points, we find a common scaling, $Δ\log Z = A\,\mathrm{SNR}^{n}$ with $n \simeq 1.74$--$1.95$, where the EOS contrast and binary properties determine only the prefactor $A$. This behavior follows from an Occam-factor argument, yielding $Δ\log Z \propto (Δ\tildeΛ\,\mathrm{SNR})^{2}$. Calibrating this relation on three configurations predicts, before the run, the SNR required for decisive EOS discrimination in the fourth to within $0.3\%$. These results establish a quantitative framework for assessing the EOS-discrimination reach of third-generation gravitational-wave detector networks.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies the SNR required for third-generation gravitational-wave detectors (Einstein Telescope + Cosmic Explorer) to distinguish between competing neutron star equations of state (EOS) via Bayesian evidence differences, revealing a robust power-law scaling Δlog Z ∝ SNR^n (n ≈ 1.74–1.95) governed by tidal deformability contrast and binary parameters.
AI.motivation: To determine the minimum signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) needed for third-generation gravitational-wave detectors to decisively discriminate between competing equations of state (EOS) of dense nuclear matter using tidal effects in binary neutron star inspirals.
AI.method: Bayesian nested-sampling parameter estimation on simulated binary neutron star signals observed by a network of Einstein Telescope and two Cosmic Explorer detectors; computation of Bayes evidence difference (Δlog Z) between correct and incorrect EOS models across varied SNRs, tidal deformability contrasts, mass configurations, and EOS swaps; theoretical interpretation via Occam factor analysis.
AI.result: A universal power-law scaling Δlog Z = A × SNR^n with exponent n ≃ 1.74–1.95 emerges, where prefactor A depends only on tidal deformability difference ΔΛ̃ and binary properties; Occam-factor argument predicts Δlog Z ∝ (ΔΛ̃ × SNR)²; calibration on three configurations forecasts required SNR for decisive EOS discrimination in unseen cases with <0.3% error.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes a quantitative, predictive framework for EOS-discrimination sensitivity of third-generation GW detector networks, demonstrating that Bayesian evidence differences scale robustly with SNR and tidal contrast—enabling prior forecasting of detection thresholds for nuclear physics inference.

title: From chiral to conformal anomalies: a double copy perspective for CFT correlators
summary: We uncover a double-copy relation between chiral and conformal anomalies in four-dimensional conformal field theory. We show that this relation extends from local anomaly structures to complete momentum-space three-point correlators and, through their flat-space limits, to five-dimensional scattering amplitudes. In particular, the parity-odd current correlators associated with the chiral anomaly reduce, in the flat-space limit, to a universal amplitude generated by a Chern--Simons interaction. Squaring these anomalous current correlators reproduces the contribution to the stress-tensor three-point function $\langle TTT\rangle$, controlled by the conformal anomaly, thereby establishing a direct link between chiral- and conformal-anomaly structures.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a double-copy relation between chiral and conformal anomalies in 4D CFT, linking parity-odd current correlators (chiral anomaly) to the stress-tensor three-point function (conformal anomaly) via flat-space limits and squaring—yielding a universal Chern–Simons amplitude in 5D.
AI.motivation: To uncover a structural connection between two distinct quantum anomalies—chiral (associated with current non-conservation) and conformal (associated with trace anomaly)—within the framework of four-dimensional conformal field theory and their implications for scattering amplitudes.
AI.method: Analyzes momentum-space three-point correlators of conserved currents and stress tensors in 4D CFT; computes flat-space limits to map to 5D scattering amplitudes; applies the double-copy (squaring) procedure to anomalous current correlators to reconstruct the stress-tensor correlator ⟨TTT⟩; identifies the role of Chern–Simons interactions in the resulting amplitude.
AI.result: Demonstrates that parity-odd current three-point functions encoding the chiral anomaly, upon flat-space limit, yield a universal 5D Chern–Simons scattering amplitude; their double copy reproduces exactly the conformal-anomaly contribution to ⟨TTT⟩, confirming a direct algebraic and physical link between chiral and conformal anomalies.
AI.conclusion: Chiral and conformal anomalies in 4D CFT are not independent but related by a double-copy structure—both at the level of local Weyl/BRST cohomology and full momentum-space correlators—revealing a deeper unification in quantum consistency conditions and their gravitational and higher-dimensional interpretations.

title: HiggsTools for LHC Run 3 and Beyond
summary: HiggsTools, including the subpackages HiggsPredictions, HiggsBounds, and HiggsSignals, is a toolbox for Beyond-the-SM (BSM) scalar phenomenology at the LHC. It provides BSM model predictions, tests the model against experimental limits from searches for BSM scalars and derives constraints from the measurements of the properties of the discovered Higgs boson. We present a variety of improvements to the HiggsTools framework, preparing it for the results of LHC Run 3 and the HL-LHC. HiggsPredictions now provides additional cross-section predictions for centre-of-mass energies of 13.6 and 14 TeV. Moreover, it now includes cross-section predictions for resonant and non-resonant Higgs-boson pair production. For HiggsBounds, we describe the recasting of searches using multi-top final states, explain their implementation and highlight the impact of the experimental sensitivity of those results. Furthermore, we discuss the implementation of coupling-dependent limits on non-resonant Higgs boson pair production, as well as the improved handling of searches conducted prior to the Higgs boson discovery. For HiggsSignals we describe several improvements for the case of scalars with mass uncertainties.

AI.tldr: HiggsTools—a suite comprising HiggsPredictions, HiggsBounds, and HiggsSignals—is updated to support BSM Higgs phenomenology for LHC Run 3 and HL-LHC, with enhanced cross-section predictions (including di-Higgs), recast multi-top searches in HiggsBounds, coupling-dependent limits on non-resonant di-Higgs, improved pre-discovery search handling, and better treatment of scalar mass uncertainties in HiggsSignals.
AI.motivation: To prepare the HiggsTools framework for increasingly precise LHC Run 3 and HL-LHC data, enabling robust testing of BSM scalar models against updated experimental constraints and measurements.
AI.method: Extended HiggsPredictions with new cross-section calculations at 13.6/14 TeV and resonant/non-resonant di-Higgs production; recast multi-top final-state searches and implemented coupling-dependent di-Higgs limits in HiggsBounds; improved statistical treatment of mass uncertainties in HiggsSignals.
AI.result: Enhanced predictive power and experimental compatibility: broader energy coverage, inclusion of key di-Higgs channels, more realistic exclusion limits from multi-top searches, refined handling of pre-discovery data, and robust fitting for scalars with uncertain masses.
AI.conclusion: The upgrades significantly strengthen HiggsTools’ capability to confront BSM scalar models with current and future LHC data, ensuring continued relevance for precision Higgs physics and new physics searches.

title: Asymmetric Quantum Oppenheimer-Snyder Collapse
summary: We study black hole formation resulting from the collapse of a homogeneous and isotropic dust ball within a framework built upon loop quantum cosmology. Using loop dynamics formulated for Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi spacetimes---which reduce to the asymmetric loop quantum cosmological bounce scenario---we analyze the dust ball undergoing power-law contraction followed by a de Sitter-like expansion. We discover an emergence of a physical shock at the dust ball surface, characterized by a continuous induced metric and a discontinuous extrinsic curvature arising from a dynamical mismatch between the expanding interior and the contracting exterior vacuum shells. Furthermore, we explicitly derive two variants of Schwarzschild-like line elements for the vacuum sector, and we demonstrate that the resulting spacetime is geodesically complete featuring a rich causal structure. This establishes, for the first time, fully dynamical regular black hole formation within a framework consistent with loop quantum cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first fully dynamical, regular black hole formation model consistent with loop quantum cosmology, using LTB spacetimes and loop dynamics; it reveals a physical shock at the dust-vacuum interface (continuous metric, discontinuous extrinsic curvature) and constructs geodesically complete, causally rich Schwarzschild-like vacuum geometries.
AI.motivation: To resolve the singularity problem in black hole formation by constructing a physically consistent, non-singular, fully dynamical model within loop quantum cosmology—avoiding classical singularities while preserving key quantum gravitational features.
AI.method: Applies loop quantum dynamics to Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) spacetimes modeling a collapsing homogeneous isotropic dust ball; employs asymmetric loop quantum cosmological bounce scenario; derives vacuum exterior geometry, analyzes induced metric and extrinsic curvature across the dust surface, and examines geodesic completeness and causal structure.
AI.result: Discovery of a physical shock at the dust ball surface (continuous induced metric, discontinuous extrinsic curvature) due to dynamical mismatch between bouncing interior and contracting exterior; derivation of two Schwarzschild-like vacuum line elements; demonstration of geodesic completeness and rich causal structure.
AI.conclusion: A fully dynamical, singularity-free black hole formation scenario is realized in a loop quantum cosmology–consistent framework—establishing the first such model with explicit geometry, regularity, and causal richness.

title: Information-Theoretic Black Hole Entropy I: Beyond the Area Law
summary: Although the Bekenstein-Hawking area law is consistent with the first and second laws of black hole thermodynamics, it appears to be in conflict with the third law, which in the Nernst formulation states that the entropy should either vanish or approach a universal constant in the zero-temperature limit. We argue that this tension reflects a limitation of the semiclassical area law rather than a fundamental feature of black hole thermodynamics. On this basis, we obtain an entropy formula that is consistent with the third law, and approaches Bekenstein-Hawking entropy in the high-temperature limit. The resulting entropy admits a simple microscopic interpretation, and it can be written as the Kullback-Leibler divergence between a mass-biased Bernoulli distribution and the uniform distribution on N microscopic bits. From this perspective, the thermodynamic black hole entropy admits an information-theoretic representation as an entropy deficit, namely as the relative entropy between the black hole ensemble and a maximally mixed reference ensemble. The Bekenstein-Hawking area law then emerges as the leading term in an $1/N$ expansion, while a universal mass scale $M_0=\sqrt{N}\,M_P$, interpreted as an absolute upper bound on the black hole mass, controls the bias of the underlying microscopic ensemble. The subleading terms represent finite-information corrections to the classical area law.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves the tension between black hole entropy and the third law of thermodynamics by proposing a new entropy formula—expressed as a Kullback-Leibler divergence—that vanishes at zero temperature, satisfies the Bekenstein-Hawking law asymptotically, and admits a finite-information, microscopic interpretation with an absolute mass bound M₀ = √N Mₚ.
AI.motivation: To resolve the apparent conflict between the Bekenstein-Hawking area law (which yields nonzero entropy at zero temperature) and the Nernst formulation of the third law of thermodynamics (requiring entropy to vanish or approach a universal constant as T → 0).
AI.method: Constructs a black hole entropy formula based on information-theoretic principles: interprets entropy as the Kullback-Leibler divergence between a mass-biased Bernoulli distribution over N microscopic bits and the uniform (maximally mixed) reference distribution; derives corrections to the area law via a 1/N expansion; identifies a universal mass scale M₀ = √N Mₚ as an absolute upper bound.
AI.result: A novel black hole entropy expression that (i) satisfies the third law (S → 0 as T → 0), (ii) reduces to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy in the high-temperature/large-N limit, (iii) admits a clear microscopic interpretation in terms of N binary degrees of freedom, and (iv) incorporates finite-information corrections encoded in subleading 1/N terms.
AI.conclusion: The tension with the third law stems from the semiclassical approximation's breakdown at extremality; the proposed information-theoretic entropy provides a consistent, quantum-gravitational refinement of black hole thermodynamics where the area law is emergent and approximate, and the fundamental description is governed by bounded information content and an absolute mass cutoff.

title: Spinor tunnelling amplitudes from all-order Feynman diagram summation
summary: This work presents a non-perturbative quantum field theoretic computation of spinor tunnelling through a potential barrier. Within position space potential formalism, we identify coupled recursion relations forming a self-consistent integral equation. Our method, enabling both analytical and numerical approaches, transforms into a formalism admitting both numerical framework for arbitrary potentials and analytical exact results for select barriers. For the rectangular barrier, the QFT-derived amplitudes reproduce the relativistic quantum mechanical (RQM) results, thus establishing a foundation for future calculation of beyond-RQM field-theoretic corrections.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a non-perturbative QFT method for spinor tunnelling through potential barriers using coupled recursion relations in position space, yielding exact analytical results for rectangular barriers and recovering standard RQM amplitudes—thereby enabling future computation of genuine field-theoretic corrections beyond RQM.
AI.motivation: To go beyond relativistic quantum mechanics (RQM) by computing spinor tunnelling from first-principles quantum field theory (QFT), capturing non-perturbative effects and enabling systematic calculation of field-theoretic corrections absent in RQM.
AI.method: Non-perturbative QFT formulation in position-space potential formalism; derivation of coupled recursion relations forming a self-consistent integral equation; solution via both analytical (for solvable cases like rectangular barrier) and numerical (for arbitrary potentials) approaches.
AI.result: Exact QFT-derived tunnelling amplitudes for the rectangular barrier fully agree with established RQM results; the formalism is validated and shown to be generalizable to arbitrary potentials.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully bridges QFT and tunnelling physics, reproducing RQM limits while laying groundwork for computing genuine QFT corrections—e.g., vacuum polarization, particle creation, or loop effects—in barrier penetration problems.

title: A Novel Kerr-like Black Hole in a General Double Power Law Dark Matter Environment: Geometry, Spectroscopy, and Energy Extraction
summary: We construct a novel Kerr-like black hole solution embedded in a general double power law dark matter environment by applying the Newman--Janis algorithm to a Schwarzschild-like seed geometry. This framework provides a unified rotating spacetime for arbitrary double power law density profiles and reveals how dark matter modifies the horizon structure, extremal spin, and curvature properties of rotating black holes. Remarkably, we find that the rotation--halo interplay can eliminate essential curvature singularities for Dehnen-type profiles with $γ\leq2$, despite the singular nature of the corresponding static configurations. We then investigate the spectroscopic signatures of the dark matter environment through massive scalar perturbations in the Dehnen $(1,4,γ)$ halo. Using an analytical low-frequency matching method, we derive the quasibound state spectrum, the onset condition for scalar cloud formation, and superradiant amplification factor, showing that the halo parameters $ρ_0 r_0^3$ and $γ$ leave characteristic imprints on the scalar spectrum. Increasing the halo density or the cusp strengthens the binding of quasibound states and enhances their decay, shifts the scalar cloud threshold, and suppresses superradiant amplification effectivity by narrowing the allowed frequency window and lowering the amplification factor peak. Finally, we analyze rotational energy extraction from thermal scalar fields and demonstrate that the efficiency is controlled by the interplay between the thermal spectrum and the superradiant instability, with lower temperatures and less cuspy density profiles yielding more efficient energy extraction.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a rotating (Kerr-like) black hole solution in a double power-law dark matter halo using the Newman-Janis algorithm, revealing how dark matter affects horizon structure, extremality, and curvature singularities; it further studies scalar quasibound states and superradiance in Dehnen halos, showing halo parameters imprint on spectra and suppress superradiance; finally, it analyzes rotational energy extraction from thermal scalar fields, finding efficiency depends on temperature and halo cuspiness.
AI.motivation: To unify rotating black hole spacetimes with general double power-law dark matter distributions and investigate how such environments alter fundamental black hole properties—especially singularity structure, horizon geometry, and superradiant dynamics—beyond standard vacuum Kerr physics.
AI.method: Applied the Newman–Janis algorithm to a Schwarzschild-like seed metric embedded in a double power-law dark matter profile; analytically solved massive scalar perturbations using low-frequency matching to obtain quasibound spectrum, cloud onset condition, and superradiant amplification factor; computed rotational energy extraction efficiency for thermal scalar fields via superradiant instability analysis.
AI.result: Dark matter modifies horizon radius and extremal spin; Dehnen-type halos with γ ≤ 2 eliminate curvature singularities in rotating solutions despite static singularity; halo density ρ₀r₀³ and cusp index γ imprint on scalar spectrum—increasing either strengthens binding and decay of quasibound states, shifts cloud threshold, and suppresses superradiance; thermal energy extraction efficiency is higher for lower temperatures and shallower (less cuspy) halos.
AI.conclusion: Dark matter halos fundamentally reshape rotating black hole geometry and stability: they can regularize singularities, suppress superradiant instabilities, and modulate energy extraction—making halo parameters astrophysically observable through scalar spectroscopy and superradiant signatures.

title: Information--Theoretic Black Hole Entropy II: Infrared Gravity and Charged/Rotating Extensions
summary: We investigate gravitational and Kerr-Newman extensions of an information-theoretic black-hole entropy that satisfies the Nernst formulation of the third law of thermodynamics. The entropy is identified with the Kullback-Leibler divergence between a mass-dependent Bernoulli ensemble and an unbiased reference ensemble, and therefore measures relative information rather than the logarithm of the number of black-hole microstates. We show perturbatively that its temperature and entropy can be reproduced by an infrared deformation of General Relativity. To linear order in the deformation couplings, the surface-gravity temperature and the Wald entropy agree with the information-theoretic results. In an explicit realization, the matching generates a positive effective cosmological term whose smallness is related to the large microscopic parameter $N$. We also propose an extension to Kerr-Newman black holes based on the irreducible mass. This construction preserves the connection with the horizon area and the semiclassical limit, while distinguishing geometrical extremality from the universal statistical-freezing endpoint, which is independent of angular momentum and charge.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an information-theoretic black hole entropy based on Kullback-Leibler divergence (rather than microstate counting), satisfying the Nernst version of the third law; it matches Wald entropy and surface-gravity temperature perturbatively via an IR deformation of GR, yields a small positive cosmological constant tied to large N, and extends naturally to Kerr-Newman black holes using irreducible mass.
AI.motivation: To construct a black-hole entropy formulation consistent with the Nernst (absolute-zero) version of the third law of thermodynamics, avoiding reliance on microstate counting while retaining geometric and thermodynamic consistency.
AI.method: Defines entropy as Kullback-Leibler divergence between a mass-dependent Bernoulli ensemble and an unbiased reference ensemble; employs perturbative matching to infrared-deformed General Relativity; extends to rotating-charged black holes via irreducible mass.
AI.result: The information-theoretic entropy reproduces surface-gravity temperature and Wald entropy to linear order in deformation couplings; the IR deformation generates a small positive effective cosmological constant scaling as 1/N; the Kerr-Newman extension preserves area-law behavior and semiclassical limit while distinguishing geometrical extremality from statistical freezing at zero temperature.
AI.conclusion: A relative-information–based entropy framework satisfies thermodynamic consistency—including the third law—and admits a gravitational realization via IR-modified GR; the irreducible-mass extension provides a unified statistical interpretation of extremality across black-hole families.

title: Coherent and Stochastic Axion Dark Matter from Thermal Relaxation
summary: An axion driven toward a thermal minimum need not remain a coherent condensate. We derive the coupled attenuation of the field mean and production of stochastic momentum modes in an expanding plasma. A single momentum dependent optical depth partitions every mode between coherent power and Bose occupation, placing standard misalignment, partial relaxation, and stochastic production in one dynamical relation. Finite spatial and temporal response suppresses high momentum production, so the stochastic relic has lower mean momentum and a shorter free streaming length than an equilibrium population at fixed mass and bath temperature. A weakly coupled realization produces the dark matter abundance, reduces inherited coherent isocurvature, and confines production correlations to scales removed by collisionless propagation. Thermal relaxation therefore determines the composition, momentum distribution, and transported structure of axion dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a unified dynamical framework for axion dark matter production via thermal relaxation, showing how coherent and stochastic components co-evolve in an expanding plasma; it demonstrates that finite response effects suppress high-momentum modes, yielding a colder, shorter free-streaming stochastic relic compared to equilibrium, with implications for abundance, isocurvature suppression, and structure formation.
AI.motivation: To reconcile axion dark matter production mechanisms—standard misalignment, partial relaxation, and stochastic production—within a single consistent dynamical framework accounting for thermal relaxation in an expanding plasma, and to clarify how coherence loss and stochastic mode production jointly determine the relic's composition and phase-space structure.
AI.method: Derives coupled evolution equations for the axion field mean (coherent component) and stochastic momentum modes in a thermal plasma, introducing a momentum-dependent optical depth that partitions power between coherence and Bose occupation; incorporates finite spatial and temporal response to model suppression of high-k modes.
AI.result: A unified dynamical relation linking misalignment, relaxation, and stochastic production; prediction of a non-equilibrium stochastic axion relic with suppressed high-momentum occupancy, lower mean momentum, and shorter free-streaming length than thermal expectations; quantitative reduction of coherent isocurvature and confinement of production correlations to small scales.
AI.conclusion: Thermal relaxation governs not only the abundance but also the momentum distribution and structural properties (e.g., free-streaming scale, correlation length) of axion dark matter, unifying disparate production channels and enabling testable predictions for cosmological observables.

title: A Scale-Invariant Theory of the Universe
summary: Modern physics has achieved extraordinary empirical success while retaining much of the absolute, unobservable structure introduced by Newton, largely without questioning its necessity. We investigate how far this structure can be eliminated by adopting a relational ontology guided by Leibniz's principle of sufficient reason. Removing absolute position, orientation, time and, finally, scale leads naturally to a formulation of the gravitational $N$-body problem where only dimensionless ratios are physically meaningful. Within this framework, the scale-invariant variety $V$ becomes a central quantity, providing a measure of structure, a natural ordering of shapes, and an emergent gravitational arrow of time. We argue that the resulting formulation unifies classes of Newtonian solutions previously regarded as distinct, uncovering a possible new symmetry, suggests a notion of explanation based on timeless spatial correlations rather than temporal evolution, and points towards a more economical ontology. Although developed in the context of Newtonian gravity, the principles proposed here may also offer a new perspective on general relativity and quantum mechanics.

AI.tldr: This paper explores eliminating Newtonian absolute structures (position, orientation, time, scale) via a relational ontology grounded in Leibniz’s principle of sufficient reason, leading to a scale-invariant formulation of the N-body problem where only dimensionless shape ratios are physical; the scale-invariant variety V emerges as a measure of structure, shape ordering, and gravitational arrow of time.
AI.motivation: To challenge the necessity of Newtonian absolute structures (e.g., absolute space, time, scale) by pursuing maximal relationalism guided by Leibniz’s principle of sufficient reason.
AI.method: Systematic removal of absolute degrees of freedom—position, orientation, time, and finally scale—from the gravitational N-body problem, resulting in a description purely in terms of dimensionless shape variables; analysis of the scale-invariant variety V as a geometric and dynamical quantity.
AI.result: A fully relational, scale-invariant reformulation of Newtonian gravity where physical content resides solely in dimensionless shape ratios; emergence of the scale-invariant variety V as a measure of structural complexity, natural shape ordering, and an intrinsic gravitational arrow of time; unification of previously distinct Newtonian solution classes and suggestion of a new symmetry.
AI.conclusion: Maximal relationalism eliminates redundant absolute structure, yields a more economical ontology, supports explanation via timeless spatial correlations rather than temporal dynamics, and offers conceptual insights potentially applicable to general relativity and quantum mechanics.

title: Emergent gravitational action from non-local $T\bar T$-like deformations
summary: We study the gravitational effective action induced, at first order in the deformation parameter, by non-local $T\bar T$-like deformations of quantum field theories. Using a heat-kernel formulation, we extract the local geometric terms generated by stress-tensor two-point functions, and apply the construction to free fermions, massive Maxwell theory, and second-order Yang-Mills theory. While the resulting coefficients are generally model dependent, conformal field theories contain a universal sector fixed by the central charge $C_T$. After regularization and renormalization, this sector yields finite, scheme-independent contributions organized into a finite set of curvature invariants. We further analyze trace-trace deformations, for which the relevant contact terms are determined by the Weyl anomaly, and derive the corresponding finite gravitational action for a general class of minimal non-local kernels. These results provide a quantum effective-action realization of induced gravity in which universal conformal data determine calculable contributions to the emergent geometric response.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the gravitational effective action induced by non-local $T\bar{T}$-like deformations of QFTs at first order in the deformation parameter, using heat-kernel methods and stress-tensor correlators; it identifies universal, scheme-independent curvature invariants determined solely by the central charge $C_T$ in CFTs, and extends the analysis to trace-trace deformations linked to the Weyl anomaly.
AI.motivation: To understand how non-local $T\bar{T}$-like deformations of quantum field theories induce gravitational effective actions, especially identifying universal, geometric contributions tied to conformal data (e.g., $C_T$) and connecting them to emergent gravity and the Weyl anomaly.
AI.method: Heat-kernel expansion applied to stress-tensor two-point functions; regularization and renormalization of induced geometric terms; explicit computation for free fermions, massive Maxwell, and second-order Yang-Mills; extension to trace-trace deformations using Weyl anomaly constraints and minimal non-local kernels.
AI.result: Finite, scheme-independent gravitational effective actions composed of a finite set of curvature invariants; universality of the $C_T$-dependent sector in CFTs; explicit expressions for induced gravity contributions from $T\bar{T}$-like and trace-trace deformations; contact terms fully fixed by the Weyl anomaly for the latter.
AI.conclusion: Non-local $T\bar{T}$-like deformations induce calculable, universal gravitational responses encoded in conformal data—particularly $C_T$—providing a concrete quantum effective-action realization of induced gravity where geometry emerges from QFT deformation structure.

title: Revisiting the $Λ_c^+ \to nπ^+η$ decay in light of the BESIII measurement
summary: Motivated by the latest BESIII measurements on $Λ_c^+\to nπ^+η$, we perform a systematic theoretical study of this decay. We take into account contributions from the $N(1535)$ state dynamically generated by $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson-octet baryon interactions, the $a_0(980)$ resonance originating from the $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson-pseudoscalar meson interactions, together with the intermediate states $N(1440)$ and $a_2(1320)$. Our results indicate that $a_0(980)$ provides a significant contribution to this process. The inclusion of $a_2(1320)$ hardly improves the fitting quality, while the nucleon resonances play a crucial role in describing the experimental behavior of the $π^+η$ invariant mass spectrum in both low and high energy regions. Restricted by insufficient experimental statistics and a coarse bin size of 33 MeV, the precise contribution fraction of $a_0(980)$ cannot be reliably extracted. We propose future higher-precision and higher-statistics experimental measurements of $Λ_c^+\to nπ^+η$, which can help reveal the intrinsic nature of $a_0(980)$ and quantify the roles of different excited nucleon states in this decay.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the Λc+→nπ+η decay using theoretical models incorporating resonances like N(1535), a0(980), N(1440), and a2(1320); finds a0(980) gives significant contribution, nucleon resonances crucial for π+η invariant mass spectrum, while a2(1320) adds little; calls for higher-statistics experiments to better constrain a0(980) nature and nucleon resonance roles.
AI.motivation: Motivated by recent BESIII measurements of Λc+→nπ+η, the study aims to understand underlying dynamics and resonance contributions in this charmed baryon decay.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis using hadronic effective Lagrangians and unitary coupled-channel approaches, including S-wave meson-baryon (e.g., N(1535)) and meson-meson (e.g., a0(980)) dynamically generated resonances, plus explicit N(1440) and a2(1320) contributions.
AI.result: a0(980) provides a significant contribution; N(1535) and N(1440) are essential to reproduce the π+η invariant mass spectrum across low and high energy regions; a2(1320) yields negligible improvement in fit quality; experimental limitations prevent precise quantification of a0(980)'s contribution fraction.
AI.conclusion: The decay Λc+→nπ+η is sensitive to light scalar and nucleon resonances; current data support dominant roles of a0(980) and excited nucleons, but definitive interpretation requires higher-precision experiments.

title: Coherent End-to-End Search for Generic Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) encode more than $10^5$ strong-field orbital cycles and are key targets for space-borne gravitational-wave interferometers, yet coherent recovery of generic systems over astrophysically broad priors remains unresolved. Successive Mock LISA, LISA, and Taiji Data Challenges (MLDCs, LDCs, and TDCs) have not yet produced a complete, generally reliable solution for blind EMRI detection and parameter recovery across such priors. The central obstacle is a needle-in-a-haystack likelihood: six phase-evolution parameters span a vast domain, producing an exceptionally narrow global maximum amid numerous secondary maxima. We show that higher-likelihood secondary maxima concentrate progressively around the global maximum and can therefore guide an adaptive contraction of the search volume. We exploit this structure through a reduced-dimensional profile likelihood and a coherent hierarchical strategy to search for EMRI signals across the full 14-dimensional parameter space. This enables the first end-to-end coherent parameter estimation for generic EMRIs with astrophysically broad priors. In stationary Gaussian LISA noise, the search recovers two half-year analytical-kludge signals with signal-to-noise ratios near 50, yielding fitting factors of 0.989 and 0.971, fractional errors of $10^{-3}$--$10^{-2}$ in the phase-evolution parameters and near $3\%$ in the distance, and error of less than $0.1$ radian in the sky location. The method turns secondary maxima into guides for a coherent hierarchical search.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel coherent hierarchical search method for detecting and estimating parameters of extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in LISA-like data, leveraging secondary likelihood maxima to adaptively contract the search volume across the full 14D parameter space—achieving the first end-to-end coherent parameter estimation under astrophysically broad priors.
AI.motivation: Coherent detection and parameter estimation of generic EMRIs over astrophysically broad priors remains unsolved due to the 'needle-in-a-haystack' likelihood landscape: six phase-evolution parameters produce an extremely narrow global maximum amid many secondary maxima, rendering traditional search methods ineffective.
AI.method: The authors propose a coherent hierarchical search strategy using a reduced-dimensional profile likelihood; they exploit the geometric concentration of higher-likelihood secondary maxima near the global maximum to iteratively contract the search volume in the 14-dimensional EMRI parameter space.
AI.result: The method achieves end-to-end coherent parameter estimation for generic EMRIs in stationary Gaussian LISA noise: fitting factors of 0.989 and 0.971, phase-evolution parameter fractional errors of 10⁻³–10⁻², ~3% distance error, and <0.1 radian sky-location error for two half-year analytical-kludge signals with SNR ≈ 50.
AI.conclusion: Secondary maxima in the EMRI likelihood are not nuisances but structural guides; exploiting them via adaptive, hierarchical, profile-likelihood-based search enables robust, coherent, full-parameter-space inference—resolving a longstanding challenge in EMRI data analysis for space-based GW observatories.

title: Three-Loop Five-Point CK-Dual Amplitudes and UV Structure in N=4 SYM and N=8 SUGRA
summary: We construct the complete full-color three-loop five-point integrand of N=4 super-Yang--Mills theory in a representation that manifestly satisfies color--kinematics duality. Its double copy gives the corresponding N=8 supergravity integrand. For four-dimensional external states, we evaluate the ultraviolet poles of both amplitudes in the critical dimension, Dc=6. Extending the external-state dependence to D dimensions is subtle. We consider a candidate replacement of the four-dimensional prefactors by expressions built from D-dimensional tree amplitudes. It reproduces the open-string prediction for the SYM pole with generic D-dimensional external states, whereas the corresponding gravity expression differs from the string-inspired one by an evanescent term.

AI.tldr: Constructs full-color three-loop five-point integrand for N=4 SYM satisfying color-kinematics duality; double-copies to N=8 supergravity; computes UV poles in Dc=6; tests D-dimensional extensions against string predictions.
AI.motivation: To construct a manifestly color-kinematics dual representation of the three-loop five-point amplitude in N=4 SYM and explore its double-copy relation to N=8 supergravity, while systematically addressing dimensional dependence of external states and UV behavior.
AI.method: Algebraic construction of full-color three-loop five-point integrand using BCJ-satisfying numerators; double-copy prescription to obtain N=8 supergravity integrand; dimensional regularization with evaluation of UV poles in critical dimension Dc=6; replacement of 4D prefactors by D-dimensional tree amplitudes to generalize external-state dependence.
AI.result: A manifestly color-kinematics dual integrand for N=4 SYM at three loops and five points is obtained; its double copy yields the corresponding N=8 supergravity integrand; UV poles match open-string predictions for SYM with generic D-dimensional states, but gravity exhibits an evanescent discrepancy.
AI.conclusion: The constructed integrand provides a concrete realization of color-kinematics duality at three loops for five points; the D-dimensional extension validates the SYM UV structure against string theory but reveals an evanescent ambiguity in the gravity counterpart, highlighting subtleties in dimensional continuation beyond four dimensions.

title: Net electron spin rotation in a plane-wave pulse: Holonomy set by the anomalous magnetic moment
comment: 24 pages, 4 figures, 10 tables. Single-file preprint: the article (Secs. I-VIII) followed by its Supplemental Material as an appendix (Secs. S1-S7). Submitted to Physical Review D. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21758393
summary: We compute the spin rotation that survives after a relativistic electron has crossed a plane-wave laser pulse of finite duration. In the interaction picture built on the exact $g=2$ evolution, the Thomas-Bargmann-Michel-Telegdi equation becomes parallel transport by a connection with constant coefficients on the polarization plane, and the pulse enters only through the closed curve that the transverse vector potential traces there. The net rotation is the holonomy of that connection: an angle $-\frac{1}{2}a_e^2\mathcal{A}$ about the propagation direction, with $a_e=(g-2)/2$ the anomaly and $\mathcal{A}$ twice the signed area enclosed by the curve. That area is the spin angular momentum the pulse carries per unit area, so the rotation measures the helicity of the light. Reduction of the residual dynamics to a rotation coupled through the anomaly alone is an exact result of the 1960s [Ternov, Bagrov, and Klimenko, Sov. Phys. J. 11, 29 (1968); Bagrov and Gitman, The Dirac Equation and its Solutions (De Gruyter, Berlin, 2014), Sec. 5.3], which yields two closed-form cases; the area law is the general second order that those two cases bound. The same area governs the orientation memory of a neutral magnetic dipole [Oblak and Seraj, Phys. Rev. D 109, 044037 (2024)] with a coupling of order unity. For a charged electron on a Volkov orbit the coupling $g/2$ cancels identically, which suppresses the rotation by $1.3\times10^{-6}$ and leaves a channel with no $g$-independent part. We verify the cancellation at $g=2$ over 180 pulse configurations and the area law over 89 more. Finite focusing restores that part at second order in $1/kw_0$, and it exceeds the anomalous signal unless $w_0\gtrsim16λ$ at $γ=10$, or $270λ$ at $γ=1$.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the spin rotation of a relativistic electron after traversing a finite-duration plane-wave laser pulse, showing it is governed by a geometric holonomy—the enclosed area of the transverse vector potential curve—scaled by the electron’s magnetic anomaly $a_e$, and reveals exact cancellation of the leading-order $g$-independent spin rotation for $g=2$ in plane waves, restored only upon finite focusing.
AI.motivation: To resolve how electron spin rotates under intense laser fields beyond the dipole approximation, especially clarifying the role of the $g$-factor, the magnetic anomaly, and light helicity in ultra-relativistic regimes where quantum electrodynamic effects become relevant.
AI.method: Uses the interaction picture based on the exact $g=2$ (Dirac) evolution; reformulates the Thomas-Bargmann-Michel-Telegdi equation as parallel transport with constant connection on the polarization plane; derives spin rotation as the holonomy (geometric phase) associated with the closed curve traced by the transverse vector potential; verifies analytic predictions numerically across 269 pulse configurations.
AI.result: The net spin rotation is $-\frac{1}{2} a_e^2 \mathcal{A}$ about the propagation axis, where $\mathcal{A}$ is twice the signed area enclosed by the transverse vector potential trajectory—equal to the pulse’s spin angular momentum per unit area (helicity density). For $g=2$, the leading $g$-independent rotation vanishes identically on Volkov orbits; finite focusing restores it at $\mathcal{O}((kw_0)^{-2})$. Numerical validation confirms cancellation at $g=2$ (180 cases) and area law (89 cases).
AI.conclusion: Spin rotation in plane-wave laser fields is a pure geometric effect tied to light helicity via the electron anomaly; the absence of $g$-independent rotation at $g=2$ reflects exact symmetry cancellation in the Volkov solution, broken only by transverse field gradients—making the effect a sensitive probe of laser beam structure and QED spin dynamics.

title: Radial spectra and dynamical signatures of excited boson stars
summary: We compute the lowest radial mode of spherically symmetric boson stars along equilibrium branches with a fixed number of radial nodes, considering both mini boson stars and quartically self-interacting models. By reformulating the pulsation equations in additive variables that remain regular at the zeros of the background scalar field, the eigenvalue problem can be integrated directly through the nodes of excited configurations. For all branches examined, the first zero of the constrained fundamental radial eigenvalue coincides, within numerical resolution, with the first simultaneous critical point of the Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) mass, Noether charge, and binding energy. We further evaluate the radial eigenvalue for the threshold models identified in nonlinear spherical evolutions of excited boson stars and find a simple empirical correlation with the node number and self-interaction strength. Our results provide a regular perturbative framework for excited boson stars and clarify the relation between constrained radial modes, equilibrium critical points, and nonlinear stability diagnostics.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the lowest radial mode of spherically symmetric boson stars across equilibrium branches with fixed radial node numbers, using a regular reformulation of pulsation equations to handle zeros of the scalar field; it finds that the first zero of the fundamental constrained radial eigenvalue aligns with critical points of ADM mass, Noether charge, and binding energy, and establishes an empirical correlation between eigenvalues and node number/self-interaction strength.
AI.motivation: To establish a regular perturbative framework for excited boson stars and clarify the relationship among constrained radial modes, equilibrium critical points, and nonlinear stability diagnostics.
AI.method: Reformulating pulsation equations in additive variables regular at scalar field zeros, enabling direct integration through nodes; computing constrained fundamental radial eigenvalues along equilibrium branches for mini and quartically self-interacting boson stars; comparing eigenvalue zeros with critical points of ADM mass, Noether charge, and binding energy; evaluating eigenvalues for threshold models from nonlinear spherical evolutions.
AI.result: The first zero of the constrained fundamental radial eigenvalue coincides numerically with the first simultaneous critical point of ADM mass, Noether charge, and binding energy across all examined branches; an empirical correlation is found between the radial eigenvalue and both node number and self-interaction strength.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a robust, regular perturbative method for analyzing excited boson stars and confirms a tight correspondence between linear mode structure, equilibrium thermodynamic criticality, and nonlinear stability thresholds.

title: Machine Learning is Good for Physics - and Vice Versa
summary: Scientific AI is rapidly transforming fundamental physics research and challenging defining aspects of the fundamental physics methodology. We discuss opportunities and dangers of this transformation and find exciting benefits from a close interaction between AI and fundamental physics, provided that we remain aware of the scientific methodologies of the respective fields. For fundamental physics, we discuss two such aspects: statistical validation and a generalizing theory description, both with the goal of discovering new physics in vast datasets.

AI.tldr: This paper examines how Scientific AI is reshaping fundamental physics research, highlighting synergies and methodological risks—particularly concerning statistical validation and theory generalization for discovering new physics in large datasets.
AI.motivation: To address the transformative impact of Scientific AI on fundamental physics methodology and to identify opportunities and pitfalls in integrating AI with physics-driven discovery.
AI.method: Conceptual analysis and critical discussion of two core methodological aspects—statistical validation and generalizing theory description—in the context of AI-assisted physics discovery.
AI.result: Identifies mutual benefits from AI–physics collaboration but stresses the necessity of preserving domain-specific scientific rigor, especially in statistical inference and theoretical abstraction.
AI.conclusion: A productive integration of AI and fundamental physics is possible only if both fields respect and complement each other’s methodological foundations.

title: Quasinormal Modes of Gauss--Bonnet Black Holes via the Spectral Method: Scalar, Vector, and Tensor Perturbations
summary: We present a unified study of scalar, vector, and tensor quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Schwarzschild black holes corrected by a Gauss--Bonnet (GB) term in higher dimensions. Using a high-precision Chebyshev spectral method, we map the QNM spectra across $D\in\{5,6,7,8,10,11,12,26\}$ well beyond the regime where sixth-order WKB and characteristic-integration techniques remain reliable. Across the three spin sectors, we find several robust signatures of higher-curvature dynamics: the appearance of overdamped purely imaginary modes, non-monotonic behaviour in the real parts of higher overtones, and a strong amplification of the dimensionless QNM frequencies in string-motivated dimensions. In the scalar and vector sectors, we uncover an exact isospectrality between the scalar monopole ($\ell=0$) and vector dipole ($\ell=1$) at vanishing GB coupling, and we provide an analytic proof based on a Darboux factorisation of the corresponding Hamiltonians. In the tensor sector, we obtain the first numerical confirmation of the long-predicted instability in six dimensions; its onset is sharply captured by the Cohn--Calogero bound and leads to the mass threshold $GM\leq 158.1\,α^{3/2}$. No analogous instability is found for $D\geq 7$, and no tensor isospectrality occurs. Converting the dimensionless frequencies to physical units suggests that the amplified modes in higher dimensions may enter the sensitivity window of future space-based detectors such as DECIGO. The merged analysis provides a comprehensive benchmark for QNMs in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and highlights the limitations of standard approximation schemes in the strong-coupling and high-overtone regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts a high-precision numerical study of scalar, vector, and tensor quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Schwarzschild black holes in Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity across 8 spacetime dimensions (D = 5 to 26), revealing novel spectral features—including overdamped modes, non-monotonic overtones, and dimension-dependent amplification—and proving exact isospectrality between scalar ℓ=0 and vector ℓ=1 modes at zero GB coupling; it confirms the six-dimensional tensor instability with a precise mass threshold and benchmarks limitations of WKB/characteristic methods.
AI.motivation: To systematically characterize QNMs of Schwarzschild black holes in Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity across diverse dimensions, test theoretical predictions (e.g., tensor instability in D=6), assess validity of approximation schemes (WKB, characteristic integration), and explore phenomenological relevance for gravitational-wave detectors.
AI.method: High-precision Chebyshev spectral method applied to master equations for scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations; analytic Darboux factorisation to prove isospectrality; use of Cohn–Calogero bound to locate instability threshold; dimensional conversion to physical units for detector sensitivity estimation.
AI.result: Discovery of robust higher-curvature signatures: overdamped purely imaginary modes, non-monotonic real parts of higher overtones, and strong amplification of dimensionless QNM frequencies in string-motivated dimensions (e.g., D=10,11); exact isospectrality between scalar ℓ=0 and vector ℓ=1 modes at α=0; first numerical confirmation of D=6 tensor instability with GM ≤ 158.1 α^{3/2}; no instability or isospectrality found for D ≥ 7; amplified modes potentially detectable by DECIGO.
AI.conclusion: The unified QNM analysis establishes a high-fidelity benchmark for Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet black holes, exposes breakdowns of standard approximation techniques in strong-coupling and high-overtone regimes, and identifies distinctive spectral fingerprints—especially in D=6 and string-theoretic dimensions—that could guide future tests of higher-curvature gravity with gravitational-wave observations.

title: Descoped and Upscoped FCC-ee Running Scenarios in the SMEFT
summary: We present projections for the sensitivity to new physics of descoped and upscoped FCC-ee scenarios in the framework of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). Starting from the baseline FCC-ee programme, we analyse the subsequent impact of, first, removing the top-quark run, then reducing the beam power from 50 MW to 30 MW, and finally removing two interaction points (IPs), in all cases propagating the resulting loss in top-quark mass precision through increased parametric uncertainties. We also analyse the possibility of a staged top-quark run, where the top-quark run is partially restored in case funding becomes available only at a later stage. Motivated by the trade-off between beam power and operational costs, we also consider two upscoped scenarios, either through a uniform increase in luminosity across all energy runs, or through a luminosity enhancement targeting exclusively the top-quark run. We explore the sensitivity and limitations of each scenario and highlight in particular the complementarity between the FCC-ee projections and the (HL)-LHC measurements. By comparing the physics impact of the different running scenarios with the FCC-ee baseline, we show explicitly the importance of the top-quark run, indicating that a substantial fraction of the FCC-ee physics potential depends on it.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates how descoped and upscoped FCC-ee running scenarios affect sensitivity to new physics within SMEFT, emphasizing the critical role of the top-quark run and its interplay with luminosity, beam power, and interaction points.
AI.motivation: To quantify the physics impact—especially SMEFT sensitivity—of various FCC-ee operational configurations (e.g., descoping top-quark run, reducing beam power or IPs, or upgrading luminosity), and assess trade-offs between cost, feasibility, and discovery potential.
AI.method: SMEFT global fit analysis using projected experimental uncertainties; systematic propagation of parametric uncertainties—particularly top-quark mass—from changes in beam power (50 MW → 30 MW), removal of top-quark run and/or interaction points, and staged or enhanced luminosity scenarios.
AI.result: Top-quark run is essential: its removal significantly degrades SMEFT sensitivity; staged restoration partially recovers physics reach; upscoped luminosity—especially top-targeted—improves constraints; FCC-ee projections are highly complementary to (HL)-LHC.
