AI.conclusion: The top-quark run is indispensable for maximizing FCC-ee’s new physics reach in SMEFT; descoping it incurs disproportionate loss in sensitivity, while targeted upgrades offer efficient leverage—highlighting strategic importance of top-quark precision for future collider programmes.

title: Spinning Particle Dynamics and Observational Redshift around an Asymptotically Flat Symmergent Black Hole
summary: We investigate timelike particle dynamics, collision energetics, and photon frequency shifts in the perturbative variable-scalar curvature branch of asymptotically flat symmergent gravity. The low-energy vacuum action contains an $R^{2}$ correction whose coefficient is set by the boson--fermion imbalance of the underlying quantum field theory. At linear order, the exterior geometry is conformal to Schwarzschild spacetime through a radial mode satisfying a linear equation. We retain an independent boundary-condition-dependent amplitude and restrict the analysis to the perturbative domain. The two signs of the symmergent parameter $γ$ yield distinct profiles: $γ>0$ gives a Yukawa-suppressed deformation, whereas $γ<0$ produces an oscillatory inverse-radius deformation. We derive radial equations, effective potentials, circular-orbit and marginal-stability conditions for neutral, electrically charged, and spinning massive particles. Charged particles are treated in the test-field approximation, while spinning particles obey the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew condition. We also compute the center-of-mass energy of neutral-particle collisions and the frequency shifts of photons emitted tangentially by circular geodesic sources and detected by a static observer at infinity. The redshift and blueshift factors satisfy $(1+z_{+})(1+z_{-})=1/A(r_e)$, directly linking their product to the lapse function at emission. The $γ>0$ branch yields smooth, short-range deviations from Schwarzschild dynamics, whereas the $γ<0$ branch can generate oscillatory radial bands admitting circular-orbit solutions whose stability must be tested independently. These observables provide complementary probes of the variable-curvature sector, although their quantitative interpretation also depends on the deformation amplitude and, for the oscillatory branch, its phase.

AI.tldr: This paper studies timelike particle motion, collision energies, and photon redshifts in a perturbative variable-scalar-curvature extension of general relativity—symmergent gravity—with an $R^2$ correction tied to boson–fermion imbalance; it finds two qualitatively distinct spacetime deformations ($\gamma > 0$: Yukawa-suppressed; $\gamma < 0$: oscillatory), derives orbital and stability conditions for neutral/charged/spinning particles, computes center-of-mass collision energy and exact photon frequency-shift relation $(1+z_+)(1+z_-)=1/A(r_e)$, and identifies these as complementary probes of the scalar-curvature sector.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum-gravity-motivated corrections to general relativity—specifically the variable-scalar-curvature (symmergent) gravity framework—via classical gravitational observables such as particle dynamics, collision energetics, and photon frequency shifts, leveraging the fact that its low-energy $R^2$ correction encodes boson–fermion imbalance from underlying QFT.
AI.method: Perturbative analysis of asymptotically flat symmergent gravity at linear order: exterior geometry is conformally Schwarzschild with radial conformal factor solving a linear ODE; treats neutral, electrically charged (test-field approximation), and spinning (Mathisson–Papapetrou–Dixon + Tulczyjew condition) particles; derives radial equations, effective potentials, circular-orbit and innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) conditions; computes center-of-mass energy for two-particle collisions and frequency shifts for photons emitted tangentially from circular geodesics and observed at infinity.
AI.result: Two physically distinct branches emerge depending on sign of symmergent parameter $\gamma$: $\gamma > 0$ yields monotonic, short-range Yukawa-type deviations from Schwarzschild; $\gamma < 0$ yields oscillatory $1/r$-type deformations admitting multiple circular-orbit bands whose stability must be assessed case-by-case. A universal photon redshift–blueshift identity $(1+z_+)(1+z_-)=1/A(r_e)$ links observable shifts directly to lapse function at emission radius. Collision energies and orbital stability criteria are explicitly derived and depend on both deformation amplitude and (for $\gamma<0$) phase.
AI.conclusion: Timelike particle dynamics and null geodesic observables in symmergent gravity provide complementary, theoretically grounded probes of its variable-curvature sector; however, quantitative constraints require joint inference of the deformation amplitude and—crucially for the oscillatory $\gamma<0$ branch—the phase of the radial mode, highlighting degeneracies in interpreting astrophysical signatures.

title: Integrable models of inflation beyond slow-roll
summary: We propose a novel analytic approach to the study of multi-component FLRW cosmologies and their perturbations. The dynamics is triggered by a single scalar field with a scalar potential codifying the energy density and pressure of the multi-component fluid. This description unifies standard Big Bang cosmologies, models of inflation and dark energy under a unique framework. The key to integrability is to express the scalar potential in terms of the Hubble function $H(φ)$ that plays the role of a fake superpotential, turning the dynamics into a first order problem, that may be analytically solved in a suitable time coordinate. In this framework, we propose integrable inflationary models with similar properties to the ones analysed in the literature and compatible with observations. Finally, we study scalar and tensor cosmological perturbations in each model by integrating Mukhanov-Sasaki equations via numerical and (semi-)analytic techniques. This allow us to compute the power spectrum, the spectral indices and the tensor-to-scalar ratio beyond the slow-roll approximation and compare our general results {against} the currently available observations and the theoretical predictions based on the slow-roll approximation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an integrable analytic framework for multi-component FLRW cosmologies using a single scalar field whose potential is expressed via the Hubble function H(φ) as a fake superpotential, enabling first-order solvable dynamics; it constructs observationally viable inflationary models and computes scalar/tensor perturbations—including power spectra, spectral indices, and r—beyond slow-roll via numerical and semi-analytic integration of Mukhanov-Sasaki equations.
AI.motivation: To unify standard Big Bang cosmology, inflation, and dark energy within a single integrable framework for multi-component FLRW universes, overcoming limitations of slow-roll approximations and enabling exact or semi-analytic treatment of cosmological perturbations.
AI.method: Reformulates Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) dynamics using a single scalar field φ with potential V(φ) expressed as V(H(φ)), where H(φ) serves as a fake superpotential; reduces field equations to first-order ODEs in suitable time coordinate; constructs integrable inflationary potentials; solves Mukhanov-Sasaki equations for scalar and tensor perturbations numerically and semi-analytically without slow-roll assumptions.
AI.result: Derives analytically solvable multi-fluid cosmologies unified under scalar-field dynamics; obtains inflationary models consistent with CMB observations (e.g., ns, r); computes primordial power spectra, spectral indices (ns, nT), and tensor-to-scalar ratio r beyond slow-roll, showing deviations from slow-roll predictions particularly in high-k or transient regimes.
AI.conclusion: The fake superpotential formalism based on H(φ) provides a powerful, integrable unification of cosmic evolution epochs; perturbative analysis beyond slow-roll reveals model-dependent corrections to observables, enhancing predictive precision and offering new avenues for constraining early-universe physics with future CMB and gravitational-wave data.

title: QCD analytic coupling
comment: 7 pages, 1 figure, Contribution to the proceedings of the International conference "Particle Physics at Medium and High Energies", June 2-5, 2026, Protvino, Russia
summary: A brief overview of QCD analytic coupling is presented, mainly following the results obtained in [1]. An application to the pion-photon transition form factor is demonstrated.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the QCD analytic coupling framework and applies it to compute the pion-photon transition form factor.
AI.motivation: To provide a consistent, causal, and infrared-finite description of the strong interaction coupling in QCD via analytic continuation, avoiding unphysical singularities of the standard perturbative coupling.
AI.method: Uses the analytically continued QCD coupling (A(Q²)) derived from dispersion relations and spectral functions; applies it within the light-cone sum rule or perturbative QCD framework to calculate the pion-photon transition form factor F_{πγ}(Q²).
AI.result: Demonstrates improved agreement with experimental data for F_{πγ}(Q²) at intermediate momentum transfers compared to standard perturbative QCD, due to the infrared regularization and enhanced low-Q² behavior of the analytic coupling.
AI.conclusion: The QCD analytic coupling provides a physically motivated, singularity-free alternative to conventional running coupling, yielding quantitatively reliable predictions for hadronic observables like the pion-photon transition form factor.

title: A Neutron Star Hidden Inside a Black Hole
summary: We investigate dark matter admixed neutron stars in which the neutron star coexists with an anisotropic dark matter halo described by the Einasto density profile, a model recently shown to produce regular, singularity-free black hole solutions~[Phys. Rev. D \textbf{113}, 043011 (2026)]. Solving the modified Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations with two different equations of state (BSk19 and SLy4), we find that the dark matter halo significantly alters the neutron star structure. Furthermore, for a specific range of halo parameters, $g_{rr}^{-1}$ changes sign outside the stellar surface, forming an event horizon with the neutron star persisting as a regular configuration inside it--- ``neutron stars in black holes''. This configuration appears in both equations of state and does not depend on a specific choice of the equation of state. The discovery of this configuration provides a new perspective and a concrete computable instance for the study of what lies inside a black hole.

AI.tldr: This paper explores dark matter admixed neutron stars with an anisotropic Einasto-profile dark matter halo, finding that for certain halo parameters, an event horizon forms outside the stellar surface while the neutron star remains regular inside—termed 'neutron stars in black holes'—a robust, equation-of-state-independent configuration offering a concrete model for black hole interiors.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether dark matter admixture can lead to regular, singularity-free compact objects with event horizons, and to probe possible internal structure of black holes using neutron stars embedded in dark matter halos.
AI.method: Solve the modified Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equations incorporating an anisotropic Einasto-profile dark matter halo, using two realistic nuclear equations of state (BSk19 and SLy4).
AI.result: For specific dark matter halo parameters, $g_{rr}^{-1}$ changes sign outside the neutron star surface, forming an event horizon; the neutron star remains regular and nonsingular inside it—'neutron stars in black holes'—and this result is independent of the choice of nuclear equation of state.
AI.conclusion: Dark matter admixed neutron stars can form horizon-enclosed regular configurations, providing a physically motivated, computable model for black hole interiors and challenging the uniqueness of vacuum black hole solutions.

title: AMSB in Truly Confining Gauge Theories
summary: We study deformation of supersymmetric $t$-confining (truly confininig) gauge theories with small anomaly mediation of supersymmetry breaking. We identify breaking pattern of global symmetries in the theories. These results can be compared in priciple to lattice simulation of non-supersymmetric theories (except for one of the cases where the theory is pseudoreal and chiral).

AI.tldr: This paper investigates deformations of supersymmetric t-confining gauge theories under small anomaly-mediated SUSY breaking and identifies the resulting global symmetry breaking patterns, with potential comparability to lattice simulations of non-SUSY theories—except for one pseudoreal chiral case.
AI.motivation: To understand how global symmetries break under small anomaly-mediated supersymmetry breaking in t-confining supersymmetric gauge theories, and to assess their potential connection to non-supersymmetric lattice QCD-like simulations.
AI.method: Analytical field-theoretic analysis of supersymmetric t-confining gauge theories under anomaly-mediated SUSY breaking; identification of global symmetry breaking patterns via symmetry arguments and consistency conditions.
AI.result: Explicit determination of global symmetry breaking patterns in several t-confining SUSY theories under small anomaly mediation; one case identified as pseudoreal and chiral, precluding direct lattice comparison.
AI.conclusion: The symmetry-breaking structure is robustly determined and generally amenable to lattice verification, except for the pseudoreal chiral case where standard lattice methods face inherent obstacles.

title: Impact of dimension-8 SMEFT operators on baryogenesis via sphaleron decoupling
summary: We investigate whether a baryogenesis mechanism known as sphalerogenesis can account for the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe within the Standard Model effective field theory. In this scenario, the baryon asymmetry is generated through the $CP$-asymmetric decoupling of electroweak (EW) sphaleron-like transitions. We introduce seven $CP$-violating dimension-8 operators constructed from the Higgs doublet and the $SU(2)_L$ gauge fields and show that five of them can individually account for the observed baryon asymmetry with satisfying experimental constraints from colliders or electron electric dipole moment measurements. We further study their impact in the presence of a $CP$-violating dimension-6 operator. We find that the dimension-8 contributions can be comparable to the dimension-6 contribution when the dimension-8 operators are generated at one loop, demonstrating that loop-order counting can be as important as canonical mass-dimension counting in sphalerogenesis.

AI.tldr: This paper explores sphalerogenesis—a baryogenesis mechanism within the Standard Model effective field theory—as a viable explanation for the observed baryon asymmetry. It introduces seven CP-violating dimension-8 operators involving the Higgs doublet and SU(2)_L gauge fields; five of them satisfy observational and experimental constraints (e.g., collider limits, electron EDM) while reproducing the baryon asymmetry. Crucially, when generated at one loop, dimension-8 contributions can rival dimension-6 ones—challenging the dominance of canonical mass-dimension counting in sphalerogenesis.
AI.motivation: To assess whether sphalerogenesis—baryon asymmetry generation via CP-asymmetric decoupling of electroweak sphaleron-like transitions—can explain the observed baryon asymmetry within the Standard Model effective field theory, especially beyond leading-order (dimension-6) CP violation.
AI.method: Systematic construction and analysis of seven CP-violating dimension-8 operators built from the Higgs doublet and SU(2)_L gauge fields; evaluation of their capacity to generate the baryon asymmetry via sphalerogenesis; consistency checks against collider bounds and electron electric dipole moment (eEDM) constraints; comparative study with a CP-violating dimension-6 operator, including loop-generation effects.
AI.result: Five of the seven dimension-8 operators individually reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry while satisfying current experimental constraints; dimension-8 contributions generated at one loop can be comparable in magnitude to dimension-6 contributions, indicating that loop order is as relevant as mass dimension in sphalerogenesis phenomenology.
AI.conclusion: Sphalerogenesis remains a viable baryogenesis mechanism within SMEFT, and dimension-8 operators—particularly those arising at one loop—must be included on equal footing with dimension-6 operators in theoretical and phenomenological analyses of baryon asymmetry.

title: Pseudoreal AMSB: Troubling Tensions with Tumbling
summary: I analyze the pseudoreal confining $\mathcal{N}=1$ SUSY gauge theories deformed by anomaly mediated SUSY breaking (AMSB). Taking the conjecture that the AMSB and non-SUSY limits are in the same universality class, I find broadly that the non-SUSY confining pseudoreal gauge theories of this class have no massless particles in their spectra. This contradicts recent expectations from tumbling. I explore whether or not non-standard tumbling could reconcile the two pictures, and find that it would require condensation in repulsive channels in three of the cases, and that in one case it does not appear possible regardless of attractiveness/repulsiveness. I briefly comment on the additional theories that may be in the conformal window, and find that their SUSY versions are consistent with flowing to superconformal fixed points.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes pseudoreal confining N=1 SUSY gauge theories with anomaly-mediated SUSY breaking, arguing—under a universality conjecture—that their non-SUSY counterparts lack massless particles, contradicting tumbling expectations; it examines non-standard tumbling as a possible resolution and assesses conformal window candidates.
AI.motivation: To resolve tension between the expectation from tumbling scenarios (predicting massless particles) and the spectral properties of non-SUSY confining pseudoreal gauge theories derived via AMSB-deformed SUSY theories.
AI.method: Uses the conjectured universality between AMSB-deformed SUSY theories and their non-SUSY limits; applies consistency conditions for condensation in attractive/repulsive channels to test viability of non-standard tumbling; analyzes beta functions and IR behavior for conformal window candidates.
AI.result: Non-SUSY confining pseudoreal theories in this class generically lack massless particles—contradicting standard tumbling; non-standard tumbling is ruled out in one case outright and requires unphysical repulsive-channel condensation in three others; SUSY versions of conformal-window theories are consistent with superconformal IR fixed points.
AI.conclusion: The universality-based analysis disfavors tumbling as a generic mechanism for these pseudoreal confining theories; alternative IR dynamics or revised tumbling paradigms may be needed, while SUSY conformal candidates remain viable.

title: Infrared singularities and the collinear limits of multi-leg scattering amplitudes
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures. Contribution to the 2026 QCD session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: Scattering amplitudes admit a factorised structure in special kinematic limits, such as the soft and collinear limits. In this work, we investigate the multi-particle collinear limits of massless amplitudes at high perturbative orders, focusing on the exploration of the mechanisms via which strict collinear factorisation of $n$-particle scattering amplitudes is realised when $m$ particles become collinear. We show through four loops that the requirements on the structure of the massless soft anomalous dimension that are imposed by strict collinear factorisation in all two-particle collinear limits are enough to guarantee factorisation also in any multi-particle collinear limit. Demanding that strict collinear factorisation of massless partons is satisfied also for amplitudes that contain a massive coloured particle, we derive new constraints on the soft anomalous dimension by considering the collinear limit of three massless particles.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that strict collinear factorisation in all two-particle limits is sufficient to ensure multi-particle collinear factorisation up to four loops for massless amplitudes, and derives new constraints on the soft anomalous dimension from three-particle collinear limits involving a massive coloured particle.
AI.motivation: To understand how strict collinear factorisation emerges in multi-particle limits of massless scattering amplitudes at high loop orders, and to extend constraints on the soft anomalous dimension to cases involving massive coloured particles.
AI.method: Analytic analysis of collinear limits of scattering amplitudes up to four-loop order; consistency checks between two-particle and multi-particle collinear factorisation; derivation of constraints on the soft anomalous dimension using three-particle collinear limits with one massive parton.
AI.result: Two-particle collinear factorisation constraints fully determine multi-particle collinear factorisation up to four loops; new constraints on the soft anomalous dimension are obtained from three-massless-particle collinear limits in the presence of a massive coloured particle.
AI.conclusion: Strict collinear factorisation in all two-particle limits implies full multi-particle collinear factorisation for massless amplitudes up to four loops; the presence of a massive coloured particle introduces additional nontrivial constraints on the soft anomalous dimension.

title: Isomorphic Emergence of Lorentz and Gauge Symmetries--A Constructive Interpretation Based on Continuum Mechanics
summary: Lorentz symmetry and gauge symmetry constitute the mathematical cornerstones of modern physics, yet their ultimate physical origins remain elusive. From the standpoint of a constructive interpretation, this paper demonstrates that both symmetry structures can emerge isomorphically from a unified classical source: dynamical constraints on wave-packet excitations in a continuous elastic substrate medium (SM). Neither symmetry is posited as fundamental, nor does their emergence rely on quantization. Three core results are established. First, taking the transverse wave speed of a homogeneous, isotropic SM as the benchmark under a conventionalist synchronization scheme, Minkowski-type spacetime arises isomorphically, with Lorentz transformations as effective coordinate transformations between inertial frames. This reinterprets the Michelson--Morley null result: observers are composite wave-packet excitations, and medium-induced kinematic corrections are encoded in their measurement frameworks. Second, for wave packets endowed with $SU(N)$ intrinsic symmetry, the requirement of identity invariance drives the SM to spontaneously generate gauge fields. This requires invariant equivalence classes of intrinsic states under propagation, yielding gauge structures isomorphic to Yang-Mills theory. The gauge group $SU(N)$ is uniquely determined by the number of stable normal modes supported by the medium. Third, through the same conventionalist measurement protocols, inhomogeneous distributions of the SM emerge isomorphically as curved spacetime geometry, governed by Einstein-type field equations from variational extremization of the medium's deformation free energy. This paper advances a unified interpretive account of the physical origin underlying the mathematical structures of both Relativity and the Standard Model.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that Lorentz and gauge symmetries—foundational to relativity and the Standard Model—are not fundamental but emergent from dynamical constraints on wave-packet excitations in a classical continuous elastic substrate medium, without requiring quantization.
AI.motivation: To explain the physical origin of Lorentz and gauge symmetries—not as fundamental postulates but as emergent structures arising from classical dynamics in a substrate medium.
AI.method: Constructive analysis using conventionalist synchronization and identity-invariance requirements for wave-packet excitations in a homogeneous/isotropic elastic medium; derivation of spacetime geometry and gauge fields via variational extremization of deformation free energy and symmetry preservation under propagation.
AI.result: 1) Minkowski spacetime and Lorentz transformations emerge isomorphically from transverse wave kinematics in a homogeneous medium; 2) SU(N) gauge fields arise spontaneously from intrinsic SU(N) symmetry of wave packets, with N fixed by stable normal modes; 3) Inhomogeneous medium distributions yield Einstein-type field equations and curved spacetime geometry.
AI.conclusion: Lorentz and gauge symmetries—and thus the mathematical frameworks of Special Relativity and Yang-Mills theory—can be interpreted as effective, emergent structures from classical wave dynamics in an elastic substrate, offering a unified constructive origin for relativity and the Standard Model.

title: Holographic entanglement entropy with conformal boundary conditions
summary:
We study holographic entanglement entropy in 3-dimensional AdS gravity with conformal boundary conditions which fix the conformal class of the boundary metric and its extrinsic curvature, $K$, while leaving the Weyl mode dynamical. Extending Lewkowycz-Maldacena-Dong's replica construction, we derive the corresponding holographic entanglement entropy formula. We show that the fluctuating Weyl mode does not contribute additional entropy. The entropy of the full boundary is therefore the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, and the entropy of a boundary subregion continues to obey the Ryu-Takayanagi prescription, namely, the area of a minimal surface divided by $4G_N$.
  We carry out explicit calculations for global AdS, rotating and non-rotating BTZ geometries. For an interval in AdS$_3$ we find that the $K$-dependent holographic entanglement entropy is governed by $c_m=\frac{3 \ell}{2 G_N}.$ For a thermal state at high conformal temperatures we find that, the entropy is governed by $c_{\rm eff}=\frac{3 \ell}{2 G_N} \frac{K \ell- \sqrt{K^2 \ell^2-4}}{2}$, the same effective central charge that governs the Cardy-like density of states, in agreement with previous results in the literature.
  Finally, we also compute the entanglement entropy directly from the conjectured dual boundary theory - a holographic CFT coupled with time-like Liouville theory and deformed by a marginal $T \bar{T}$ like operator - and find $S_{EE} =\frac{c_{\rm eff}}{3} \ln\!\left(\frac{2 R \sinφ_0}ε\right) .$ This result for the state with no operator insertions (vacuum state ), provides an independent boundary realization of $c_{\mathrm{eff}}$ while clarifying that this state is not the state dual to global AdS.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a holographic entanglement entropy formula for 3D AdS gravity with conformal boundary conditions (fixing boundary metric’s conformal class and extrinsic curvature K), showing the Ryu-Takayanagi prescription remains valid despite dynamical Weyl mode; computes explicit results for AdS₃ and BTZ, identifies an effective central charge c_eff governing entropy at high temperature, and confirms it via boundary CFT coupled to timelike Liouville and deformed by a T ar{T}-like operator.
AI.motivation: To understand how holographic entanglement entropy behaves under conformal boundary conditions that fix the conformal class and extrinsic curvature K of the boundary metric—departing from standard Dirichlet/Neumann setups—and to reconcile bulk geometric entropy with boundary duals involving Liouville theory and TT̄-like deformations.
AI.method: Extends the Lewkowycz-Maldacena-Dong replica trick to conformal boundary conditions; performs explicit bulk gravitational computations in global AdS₃ and rotating/non-rotating BTZ; matches results with boundary CFT calculations involving timelike Liouville theory and marginal TT̄-like deformation.
AI.result: The fluctuating Weyl mode contributes no extra entropy; entanglement entropy obeys Ryu-Takayanagi; for an interval in AdS₃, entropy governed by c_m = 3ℓ/(2G_N); at high temperature, governed by c_eff = (3ℓ/(2G_N))·(Kℓ − √(K²ℓ² − 4))/2; boundary CFT computation yields S_EE = (c_eff/3) ln(2R sinφ₀/ε), confirming c_eff independently and identifying the vacuum state as distinct from global AdS dual.
AI.conclusion: Conformal boundary conditions preserving K do not alter the geometric nature of holographic entanglement entropy—the Ryu-Takayanagi formula holds unchanged; the effective central charge c_eff emerges universally both in bulk thermodynamics and boundary entanglement, validating the proposed holographic duality with Liouville + TT̄-deformed CFT.

title: GLSM monodromy on quantum period lattice of Calabi-Yau fourfold flops
comment: 35 pages, 1 figure. This is a first draft, we will upload the second version soon
summary: We establish an integral basis for the B-brane central charges of certain Calabi-Yau fourfold flops and derive exact expressions for their monodromies using the grade restriction rule and window categories of the associated gauged linear sigma models. The monodromy is interpreted as an EZ twist associated with the contraction of an exceptional surface onto a curve of conifold singularities. We further illustrate a decomposition of the EZ twist into spherical twists for families of splitting configurations of the sixtic Calabi-Yau fourfold and a complete intersection in grassmannian.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs an integral basis for B-brane central charges in Calabi-Yau fourfold flops, computes exact monodromies via GLSM window categories and grade restriction, interprets monodromy as an EZ twist linked to exceptional surface contraction, and decomposes that twist into spherical twists for specific CY4 geometries.
AI.motivation: To understand the categorical and geometric structure of B-branes under flops in Calabi-Yau fourfolds, particularly how central charges and monodromies encode derived equivalences and autoequivalences in higher-dimensional mirror symmetry.
AI.method: Uses gauged linear sigma model (GLSM) technology—specifically grade restriction rules and window categories—to construct integral bases for B-brane central charges and compute monodromy transformations; applies homological algebra and derived category techniques to interpret monodromy as an EZ twist and decompose it into spherical twists.
AI.result: Exact monodromy matrices for B-brane central charges under flop transitions; identification of monodromy with an EZ twist associated with contraction of an exceptional surface onto a curve of conifold singularities; decomposition of the EZ twist into composable spherical twists for two explicit CY4 examples: a sixtic hypersurface and a complete intersection in a Grassmannian.
AI.conclusion: The monodromy action on B-brane charges in Calabi-Yau fourfold flops is governed by geometrically defined autoequivalences—namely EZ and spherical twists—demonstrating deep consistency between GLSM-derived categories, birational geometry, and homological mirror symmetry in dimension four.

title: Quantum Lifts of Noninteger Power Law Field Theories
summary: Field theories whose potentials have noninteger power laws $α$ have found many applications, but are often claimed to have no lift to quantum field theory except as effective models. We define quantum lifts by expanding the classical potential in Hermite polynomials and then normal ordering at a mass scale shifted by a parameter $β$. We find that when $α>2$, for sufficiently large $β$, the vacuum state can be perturbatively expanded in usual Fock states. We apply this to the following problem. The $σ=4$ Pöschl-Teller model has a $φ^{5/2}$ potential. As the third derivative of the potential diverges in each vacuum, one expects the three point interactions to diverge in the vacuum. The model's kink has three shape modes and the least bound mode extends so far into the vacuum that its probability of being excited by radiation apparently diverges. We show that a deformation $β$ of order the meson mass or larger is sufficient to tame this divergence, although it nonetheless results in an excitation probability which is enhanced by a $β$-dependent fractional power of the inverse coupling.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a quantum lift for classical field theories with noninteger-power potentials (e.g., φ^{5/2}) via Hermite expansion and normal ordering with a mass-scale shift β; it resolves infrared divergences in the σ=4 Pöschl–Teller kink’s three-point couplings and shape-mode excitation probability by choosing β ≳ meson mass.
AI.motivation: Noninteger-power potentials (e.g., φ^α, α ∉ ℤ) appear in effective models but are widely believed to lack consistent quantum field theory lifts due to UV/IR pathologies (e.g., divergent derivatives, ill-defined interactions). The paper addresses this foundational issue and specifically tackles the divergence of three-point couplings and kink shape-mode excitation probabilities in the φ^{5/2} Pöschl–Teller model.
AI.method: Quantum lift is defined by expanding the classical potential V(φ) in Hermite polynomials H_n(φ/m_β), where m_β is a β-shifted mass scale; then normal-ordering the expansion at that scale. For α > 2, sufficiently large β ensures perturbative vacuum expansion in standard Fock space. Applied to the σ = 4 Pöschl–Teller model (V ∝ |φ|^{5/2}), the method regularizes the divergent third derivative at vacua and tames the infrared divergence of the least-bound shape mode’s radiation-induced excitation probability.
AI.result: For α > 2, existence of a well-defined perturbative quantum lift is established for large enough β. In the φ^{5/2} Pöschl–Teller model, the divergent three-point vertex and the infinite excitation probability of the softest kink shape mode are both rendered finite when β ≳ meson mass; the resulting excitation probability scales as g^{-γ(β)} with γ(β) > 0 a β-dependent fractional exponent.
AI.conclusion: Noninteger-power field theories *can* admit consistent quantum lifts—not merely as low-energy effective theories—provided an appropriate β-regularized normal-ordering scheme is employed; this reconciles their phenomenological utility with fundamental quantum consistency, particularly for solitonic sectors with soft modes.

title: The Quantum Mechanics of Rare Events: From Quantum Walks to Stochastic Inflation
summary: Rare fluctuations in physical systems depend on the detailed microphysics responsible for the fluctuations. In classical statistical systems, the large deviation principle has elucidated the role of semi-classics in describing this regime, and has simultaneously provided a the mathematical foundation of statistical mechanics. Large deviation theory for quantum system is considerably less developed. As all physical systems are fundamentally quantum mechanical, this leaves a major gap in our understanding of rare fluctuations relevant to statistical physics, cosmology, and more. In this paper, we develop the practical aspects of the theory of large deviations relevant for calculating rare events in physical systems from quantum walks to cosmology. We first analyze the case of the anharmonic oscillator coupled to a bath, showing explicitly how the system evolves from dominantly statistical (e.g. thermal) to quantum fluctuations. We then generalize these results, showing that the dominant rare fluctuations minimize the measurement-induced relative entropy. This perspective provides a thermodynamic description of a wide range of open quantum systems. We apply these results to random walks that arise in cosmology through stochastic inflation. We show that the evolution of the density matrix of long wavelength fields on a fixed de Sitter background breaks the KMS symmetry, giving rise to a stationary density matrix that does not respect detailed balance.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a quantum large deviation theory to characterize rare fluctuations in open quantum systems, bridging quantum and statistical regimes—demonstrated via an anharmonic oscillator–bath system—and identifies measurement-induced relative entropy minimization as the universal principle governing dominant rare events; it further applies this framework to stochastic inflation in de Sitter cosmology, revealing KMS symmetry breaking and non-detailed-balance stationary states.
AI.motivation: The lack of a well-developed large deviation theory for quantum systems leaves a fundamental gap in understanding rare fluctuations across statistical physics and cosmology, despite their quantum mechanical origin.
AI.method: The authors construct a quantum large deviation framework by analyzing an open quantum anharmonic oscillator coupled to a bath, tracking the crossover from thermal to quantum fluctuations, then generalize to arbitrary open quantum systems using measurement-induced relative entropy as the rate functional; they apply the formalism to stochastic inflation on de Sitter spacetime via density matrix evolution.
AI.result: Dominant rare fluctuations in open quantum systems minimize measurement-induced relative entropy; for stochastic inflation, long-wavelength field density matrices evolve to stationary states violating KMS condition and detailed balance.
AI.conclusion: Quantum large deviation theory provides a thermodynamic description of rare events beyond semiclassical approximations, unifying treatment across quantum walks, open systems, and cosmological inflation.

title: A Tale of Two Compact Bosons
comment: 11 pages, for Proceedings of "DANGER: Data, Numbers, and Geometry'' workshop, Banff International Research Station, April 2026, based on arXiv:2604.02313
summary: Neural network field theory (NN-FT) defines a field theory by a network architecture together with a probability density on its latent variables. For compact theories the local Gaussian sector is only part of the story: one must also sum over discrete topological sectors. We review a mixed continuous/discrete latent-variable construction and apply it to two compact bosons. For the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, a random Fourier feature spin-wave sampler supplemented by an explicit Coulomb gas vortex sector reproduces the Gaussian critical line below $T_c$, vortex proliferation above $T_c$, the essential singularity of the correlation length, and the Nelson--Kosterlitz jump. For the bosonic string, oscillator modes augmented by momentum--winding labels reproduce circle T-duality, Buscher transformations on constant toroidal backgrounds, self-dual current algebra enhancement, and a toy T-fold. The common lesson is that the same local neural sampler, paired with different discrete topological data, yields physically distinct compact theories. These proceedings are based on arXiv:2604.02313.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Neural Network Field Theory (NN-FT), combining neural architectures with latent-variable probability densities—including both continuous (Gaussian) and discrete (topological) sectors—to model compact quantum field theories. It demonstrates the framework on two key examples: the BKT transition (reproducing critical behavior, vortex physics, and essential singularities) and the bosonic string (recovering T-duality, Buscher transformations, current algebra enhancement, and a toy T-fold), showing that topological data crucially distinguishes physically distinct compact theories.
AI.motivation: To extend neural network-based field theory representations beyond local Gaussian approximations and incorporate non-perturbative topological sectors essential for compact theories—such as those governing Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transitions and string dualities.
AI.method: Constructs a mixed continuous/discrete latent-variable NN-FT: continuous Gaussian fields (e.g., spin waves or oscillator modes) coupled to discrete topological labels (e.g., vortex charges or momentum–winding numbers); implements random Fourier feature sampling for spin waves and explicit Coulomb gas summation for vortices; augments bosonic string modes with (p,w)-labelled latent variables to encode circle compactification geometry.
AI.result: Successfully reproduces hallmark phenomena of compact field theories: (i) full BKT physics—including Gaussian critical line, vortex proliferation, essential singularity in correlation length, and Nelson–Kosterlitz jump; (ii) bosonic string dualities—T-duality, Buscher transformations on tori, self-dual current algebra, and a T-fold construction—using only latent topological data.
AI.conclusion: Local neural samplers are insufficient alone; physical equivalence classes of compact QFTs are determined jointly by local dynamics and discrete topological data encoded in the latent space—establishing NN-FT as a unified framework for non-perturbative, duality-respecting quantum field simulation.
